movements.letterExcerpt: I presume you will be greatly rejoiced to hear that I came out of the battle of the third safe and sound. I cannot be thankful enough for God's great kindness to me. The only injury I received was an ...
movements.notes: **CRITICAL** — ANTIETAM. Alexander safe, bruised knee from ball. HENRY MISSING. 34th NY man says not killed — prisoner or lost in confusion. Regiment went in 200 strong, lost 30-40.

movements.letterExcerpt: You must be very lonely since Charles has left. How did he enlist? I have been expecting a letter every day, but have been disappointed. I hope he did not go as a private, but then if he did, by being...
movements.notes: **MAJOR** — Charles enlisted; James's class standing (third section); Bible class; Prof. French; "Immortal Section"

movements.letterExcerpt: I suppose you will be both surprised and grieved to hear that I am in a hospital. I have had an exhausting diarrhea for several weeks past, which with the severest military duty has brought me pretty ...
movements.notes: **CRITICAL** — Alexander in HOSPITAL at Harpers Ferry. Exhausting diarrhea. Orderly Dickinson's kindness. Henry wounded in hand but with company (FOUND). Asks Mother for $5.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter today. I was sorry to hear about Henry. But then it may be all for the best. If he is a prisoner at Richmond as I think he is, he is safer than in our army. I think the wound in...
movements.notes: Charles responds to news of Henry's wounding. Thinks Henry is a prisoner at Richmond. Wound in leg prevented escape.

movements.letterExcerpt: It is three weeks yesterday since I left home for this place.
movements.notes: Charles to Alexander — barracks life, Henry wounded in thigh (via Shaw), thinks Henry is prisoner "with the rebels in Dixie." Most detailed description of Plattsburgh Barracks.

movements.letterExcerpt: As Alek Douglas is to leave for home tonight I send by him two pairs of socks to have the heels run as they will not last any time as they are. My new grey socks have a hole in the heel already. Perha...
movements.notes: Charles at Plattsburgh on furlough eve — sending socks, father injured by falling timber, "very likely he is a prisoner."

movements.letterExcerpt: We left for this place Monday morning at seven A.M. Arrived here at about 2 A.M. the next morning. On our arrival a large number of men were routed out of their bunks & tents for us to sleep in as the...
movements.notes: Charles's journey from Plattsburgh to Camp Mohawk (Fonda, NY) then to Alexandria. 153rd NY, Co. I. Detailed travel narrative. Assigns regiment: **153rd New York Volunteers**.

movements.letterExcerpt: It is a long, long time since I last wrote you. I know you must feel very anxious about me, but I do not think you will blame me when you know all. A day or two after I wrote you my last letter we mar...
movements.notes: Alexander's first letter since Sept 27 — 46-day gap. Has been too sick to write: jaundice, then cold, then facial eruption affecting eyes. Now at Harpers Ferry guarding government property. Capt. Ransom "very, very kind."
March to Fredericksburg area. Encamped at Falmouth.
Garrison duty at Alexandria and Capitol Hill. Guard and provost duty.
Garrison duty at Alexandria and Capitol Hill. Guard and provost duty.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter directed to Fonda some days since & have received three since, the last dated Nov. 10th I received on the 15th. We will receive our letters without being delayed, I think, after...
movements.notes: Charles's very long first letter from camp near Alexandria. 153rd NY guarding city, convalescent camp, parole camp, funeral escorts. Detailed barracks and camp life. Mathews & Leslie from Henry's Co. in Washington — not seen Henry for some time. "L. La Tube says James Beaumont died not long since of a fever." Rich is Captain, Burdick 1st Lieut. Alek Douglas's pocket book stolen ($26).

movements.letterExcerpt: How I long to see you. Wonder what you are doing today. Miss Fannie I expect is in that cozy room in the old academy (of pleasant memory to me) teaching (teaching the young ideas of how to Charles vou...
movements.notes: **THE MEETING STORY.** Alexander narrates finding Henry before Antietam — the dramatic nighttime reunion at the 34th NY camp. "Oh, how my heart bumped." Also believes Henry was "undoubtedly taken prisoner at Antietam." The 34th was "but a few hundred yards to the left of us" at Antietam.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your most welcome letter last evening and oh! how much good it has done me. There is nothing, it seems to me, that gives half the joy that a letter from home does. It is one of the stronges...
movements.notes: Alexander reflects on battle — felt Mother's prayers surrounding him under fire. Thanksgiving: bean soup and hard tack instead of Grandmother's dinner. Whiteside and Doolittle paying for substitutes. Draft criticism.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your & Mothers letter dated Nov. 20th enclosing Luthers. Glad to hear about Henry but am afraid it is too good news to be true. I should think McDonald would have written how he heard about...
movements.notes: Charles to sister Frances (Fannie). Good news about Henry from McDonald seems too good to be true. Regiment guarding different places. Frenchman from tent died. F. Borron in cavalry. Smallpox in regiment — "whole reg. has been vaxxinated." Thanksgiving on guard.

movements.letterExcerpt: I intended to have written you before & have not much excuse for not doing so, but I did not know as your address was the same & was waiting to hear from home if it was. I did not hear from home till ...
movements.notes: Charles to Alexander. Capt. Rich now on Gen. Slough's staff. Sibley tents. Henry perhaps prisoner & soon exchanged. Mother heard rumor of exchange. Two men shot fingers off accidentally. Exchanging Austrian muskets for new guns. Band instruments. McDonald to write his wife about Henry.

movements.letterExcerpt: As I am off guard today I will write to you. Guard duty at the city these cold nights is no fun. We are not allowed any guard fires now. The reason is, I suppose, that the soldiers steal all the wood ...
movements.notes: Charles's longest letter. McDonald's story about Henry "not true." Savagham heard from Mathews — brother most likely in hospital. Bethune in Capt. Rich's old Co. Saw Mathews & Leslie at Washington hospital — not seen Henry. James Beaumont died of fever. Christmas approaching. Horse beef. Paroled prisoners nearby. Chaplain description. Smallpox. Very detailed camp life.
Battle of Fredericksburg. 60th NY in reserve or lightly engaged.
Winter camp near Fairfax Station.

movements.letterExcerpt: I must "hurry up" and write or my fingers will soon be so numb that it will be wholly impossible. How I long to see you and when that will be God only knows. I wrote you a few lines the day before we ...
movements.notes: Alexander at Fairfax Station after march from Harpers Ferry via Leesburg, Hillsborough, Fairfax Courthouse, Dumfries — "twenty-four from Fredericksburg." Orders countermanded. Visited 34th NY camp — "the boys said they saw Henry grasp his leg, take a step or two, and throw himself down[?]." Believes Henry is prisoner. Pay six months overdue.

movements.letterExcerpt: I was surprised yesterday to receive a visit from Alek. Day before yesterday Capt. J. B. Ransom visited our Co. He told me then Alek stood in his first place. I asked him if he could let Alek come & s...
movements.notes: Charles's Christmas/year-end letter. Visited Alexander at Harpers Ferry before departure. Alexander jaundiced but good spirits. Christmas in camp — shoes blacked, dress parade at 4 PM. Slave men in Alexandria a "terror to our men." Washington 8 miles away. Savagham's letter not written by Tromby[?]. Only 3 men in tent of 12 can write. Charles is letter-writer for illiterate tentmates.
Joined regiment in the field near Fairfax Station.

movements.letterExcerpt: You see this letter is dated different from my other letters and the reason is our Co. has been detached from the regiment and is stationed in the city near the Potomac. Our duties, I think, will be t...
movements.notes: Charles detached from regiment, stationed in city near Potomac. Duty: returning soldiers to regiments. Visited Alexander at Fairfax Station Jan 14th[sic — date in letter]. Alexander jaundiced but well. Capt. Ransom's letter enclosed. 60th NY in 2nd Brigade, 2nd Division, 12th Army Corps. Henry "urged not to go into that fight." Mr. Rye claims land value issues.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your most welcome and long expected letter yesterday and was quite amused with one portion of it. So you think I had better roast my pork before eating, eh? Well, that will do very well whe...
movements.notes: Alexander received letter, amused by Mother's assumption of destitution. "I have seen the time when I have not had a shirt to my back or a blanket to cover myself with at night." Orders to march in 12 hours — "probably going east to reinforce Rosecrans." Commends all to God's hands.

movements.letterExcerpt: Your letter to hand making inquiry concerning Alexander's going home. I immediately applied to the commanding officer of the Regiment to have him sent home on recruiting service if any sergeant went f...
movements.notes: Captain Ransom writes to reassure Mother about Alexander. Alexander "never looked so finely and well." Visited Charles at 153rd — Charles also well. Orders to march with 12 hours notice, 11 days rations. Furlough/recruiting service "all done away with." P.S.: Charles arrived in camp; will return tomorrow at 7 AM.
With 153rd NY at DC defenses / Capitol Hill. Limited correspondence.
'Mud March' — Burnside's failed advance. Mired in mud, returned to camp.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter today and was surprised to learn that you thought I was sick. My health is very good; have got over my cough and hoarseness. Have not missed duty once on account of sickness sin...
movements.notes: Charles received pay for two months. Sent $20 allotment check. Whole Co. ordered to fall out with guns tomorrow. Guard duty at Aquia Creek — guarding soldiers. City liberty, no roll call tonight. Boy in Co. (16 years old, hard boy) absent at roll call, sent to slave pen and showered. P.S. Feb 1: Sunday, no inspection. Attended Episcopal church — "very old one of stone... buried persons who died in 1700s." Theater and circus in Alexandria.
Winter/spring camp near Aquia Landing. Drill and supply operations.

movements.letterExcerpt: Wonder if it is raining up there today as hard as it is here. It began snowing quite furiously early yesterday morning — settled down into a steady rain — rained hard a good part of yesterday, all las...
movements.notes: Alexander at Camp near Stafford House after march from Fairfax Station. Capt. Ransom gone — "much to my sorrow and the company's." Furlough application sent to War Department. Rain and mud. Lather sends regards. Short letter — no fire, cold day.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of Feb. 1st. Was glad to hear from you and also glad to read a letter so full of news. I received a letter from D. V. Savage this morning. Will answer it soon. Also one from Jam...
movements.notes: Charles writes to sister Frances. Gen. Hooker's army broken up. Pennsylvania reserves leaving. 60th NY may be retained for defense of Washington. Trip to Aquia Creek — slept on steamboat floor, visited landing. Stragglers. A. Douglas and Gokey have been to see cousin. Savagham and Charles sleep together — "short, chunky, Frenchman." Smallpox in Co. James says he has written several letters but directed them "all wrong."

movements.letterExcerpt: I arrived here safe and sound at about six P.M. yesterday. You pressed me then, that I was but fortyeight hours coming and was here six hours prior to the expiration of my furlough. Found everything h...
movements.notes: Alexander returned from furlough — arrived safe at 6 PM. Traveled: NY by NY, New Haven railroad → Springfield, Hartford, New Haven, Conn → Jersey Ferry → train to Washington. Fare: Rouse's Point to Washington $17.75. Building fortifications. "I believe this war cannot last much longer and trust I shall be home again soon."

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcome letter of Feb. 9th and also the Tribune and the Observer. I found the Tribune interesting. I'm sorry that you think I did not receive your letters. I assure you your letters ar...
movements.notes: Charles blocked by snow — 6 inches, hard and blowing. Wants $2 for boots. Went to Aquia Creek — stragglers. Trip to see Alexander at Aquia Creek on steamboat. Lieut. Col. Armstrong has difficulty with Col., has resigned. Col. under arrest. Capt. Rich to be Major. Adjutant to be Major. Does Sydney work any — does his sister or he has a boy? Funeral escorts. Dried apples unavailable.

movements.letterExcerpt: It is raining quite furiously here today and as a natural consequence we are not at work on the fortifications, much to my satisfaction. As I told you when I was at home, all I have to do is to overse...
movements.notes: Alexander at Aquia Landing. Raining — no work on fortifications. Living on road, reading novels. "Miss Fannie, hear these presentations: Frenchmen have out of the road, and your humble servant presents rather an undignified appearance." Remembers Charley and "the fat Frenchman." Mother has recovered from trip to Rouse's Point. Henry discussion — "I feel very much provoked when I think of that." Wants U.S. note.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of Feb. 23, also the Observer, in which you said Alex had been home. I was surprised to learn that he had been home. Your letter did not say much about his visit, but I intend t...
movements.notes: Charles surprised to learn Alexander had been home. Attended Episcopal Church — good sermon. Methodist churches open. Chaplain visited — "shakes hands with each one." Uncle John's letter — "he is a strong democrat and a little sesesh." Boots purchased — $4.25, sold watch for $12 to pay in 60 days. Corporal needs watch to relieve guard. Land dispute with Mr. Rye — boundary/surveyor question. Lieut. Knapp told Charles had Champlain officers visit — called for Hubbell and Staats. Citizen shot soldier; citizen arrested. Lieut. Col. Armstrong routed out of Plattsburgh. Woman living with husband in camp.

movements.letterExcerpt: I have written you two letters to your one, nevertheless, I shall write you again and expect the answers will come in due time. How do you get along now? Hope you had any sleigh rides since I left? Be...
movements.notes: Short letter. Alexander has written two letters to Mother's one. New Captain — Lieut. Delany of Co. F — "a most excellent man — one after my own heart." Direct letters to care of Capt. Delany. Both Lieutenants have resigned and gone home. Cousin Mary McNeil letter received — "quite a political dissertation and very amusing." P.S.: "You will enjoy Cousin Mary's letter up to 'ninety nine.'"

movements.letterExcerpt: I sit down to write wondering what the reason is that I don't receive a letter. Wrote you nearly three weeks since requesting that you would send me two dollars as I wished to buy a pair of boots. I t...
movements.notes: Charles visited Alexander at Aquia Creek Monday — Alex well, "very much pleased with his visit home." Alex is now 3rd sergeant, "will be second sergeant" then "promoted to Lieut." Alex looks "just as he used to — big fat face and hearty as a buck." Borrowed $2 for boots. No furloughs granted — another inspection needed. Capt. Ransom's Co. complaint — took home his Co.'s money. Freeman Bowron from Washington visiting. Alex says "it made him feel bad to see how comfortable we were." Does Richard (Resham) talk of selling?

movements.letterExcerpt: How I should like to see you both today — to be seated in your comfortable sitting room and have it snowing "pitchforks" so that we could have a nice cozy visit — something I hardly had while there. H...
movements.notes: Alexander wishes to see Mother — "snowing pitchforks." Charles came up, got boots and socks. Letter sent to Charles with money was redirected by postmaster — "sixtieth" crossed out, "Sixty first N.Y. Volunteers" written. Finished forts, now daily detail on wharves unloading boats. "Very pleasantly situated." Mrs. Hoyle sent paper with notice of Dana Lyman's death.

movements.letterExcerpt: Your letter of March 10th received; glad to hear from you. I have not heard from Alex since I saw him. He is not a good correspondent and I am not one either as I promised to write him and have not do...
movements.notes: Charles received letter from March 10. Cyrus Kellogg in squad to Aquia Creek — says Hooker will give two years more "hard fighting." Emerson Smith at convalescent camp. Henry: "I am afraid he was killed." Convalescent camp men in wooden barracks. Deserters in citizen's clothes. Henry Gregory — "too big a heart." Lieut. Burdick more a streak of blue lightning. Continuation March 20: letter from Alex with $3, sent envelope to show misdirection. Alex was well. Our regt. has shoulder scales. Tribune and Observer received. Pennsylvania men received $500 bounty. Church — Methodist, Episcopal.

movements.letterExcerpt: To you, Miss Francis, I will first address myself. I received a letter a day or two since from Mother — and none from you, but then you are, I suppose, perfectly excusable, as I believe you generally ...
movements.notes: Alexander addresses Frances directly about writing frequency. Silas Hubbell held forth at Academy — "a mighty man of valor and a great orator." "I am just about having my hair cut. It makes me think of the times when you used to box my ears." Lieut. Ingram has called. Asks Mother to follow "rules of civilized life as far as possible" — shocked at suggestion U.S. army is "an army of barbarians." 150 lbs sugar for the bush. Alma Mcyath — fulfill promise if he lives. Luther well. Regards to Captain.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of the 20th inst, a day or two since, and was much displeased with a certain part of it. Why! Mother, I am really astonished that you should say what you did: "Write the surgeon...
movements.notes: Alexander received Mother's letter of 20th. "Why! Mother, I am really astonished that you should say what you did: 'Write the surgeon to assign me a place of safety in time of battle!'" Defends his honor — "Would you have me branded as a coward?" "There is no way of settling this rebellion by the bayonet, and we can, and will do it." Loyal wealthy widow in Baltimore. Expecting pay next week. Mr. Clark caring for horse and heifer. 150 lbs sugar. Silas courting one of the Misses Crowley.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcome letter of Mch. 19th in due time. Am expecting a letter from you tomorrow. I received one from James dated Mch. 22, which I answered. He writes in good spirits. Cyrus Kellogg wa...
movements.notes: Charles received letter of Mch 19. James letter dated Mch 22 answered. Cyrus Kellogg in squad to Aquia Creek — Hooker will give "two years more hard fighting." Emerson Smith at convalescent camp. "Did Silas find out from that man at the Point about Henry. I am afraid he was killed." Convalescent camp men in wooden barracks. Lieut. Burdick wore a streak of blue lightning. Deserters. Henry Gregory — "too big a heart." Hay $2,500 a ton from Champlain. Continuation Mch 30: no letters received. Not received papers. Methodist church — crowded. Shoulder scales for regiment.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your and Frances' letter of Mch. 29th in due time. Glad to hear that you both are well. My health is very good.
movements.notes: All soldiers mustered — regiments to be filled up by draft. New Enfield rifles. Old guns scoured. Commenced target fire with blank cartridges. Freeman Bowron from Washington — un-Champlain boys visiting. "If Henry had gone to the hospital when he was sick, he might have escaped some of the battles he was in. I am afraid he was killed." Hooker's army will soon march. James "not sick of soldiering yet." Hope Co. stays here this summer. "It is too lonesome."

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of the 7 inst. a day or two since and was filled with great wrath when I read your acct. of your trouble with your sugar-maker. I fairly hopped up and down, I was so provoked. I...
movements.notes: Alexander now under marching orders — 8 days rations, 5 in knapsacks. "Army of the Potomac" was moving day before yesterday. Gen. Hooker expects "the two years men an opportunity to pay a parting salute to the rebels." **CRITICAL: Henry intelligence.** "Your intelligence about Henry fills me with sorrow, though I still hope. It is singular that we can hear of no one who saw him dead upon the field and it is upon this that I base my hope that he is yet alive. Your fears that he was wounded are groundless and (excuse me) very foolish." Mother told to tell Captain about 28 new rifles. Mrs. Hoyle sends papers — Latin sentences on wrapper.

movements.letterExcerpt: I have sent you today by express forty dollars and enclosed you will find a receipt of seven dollars and ninety cents which Ingram will call and take up which I have no fear he will do. If he does not...
movements.notes: Alexander sent $47 by express and $3 to Frilly. Received money Mother sent. Total home: $150.90. Paid Vaughan. Lieut. Ingram to send money with his. Jim doesn't want money. "How I should like to see Master James." Luther sent $20 in package. Should apply for Henry's back pay and bounty.

movements.letterExcerpt: I mailed a letter to you this morning and forgot to mention a very important matter in it. That is about a watch. Will you get me one? I need one very much. Get one with a double case. Any other would...
movements.notes: Short follow-up — forgot to mention need for a watch. "I saw one of the 34th yesterday. He inadvertently said something about Henry that pleased me very much. He said that when the boys went off and plundered anything he would not take any of it and would reason in this wise: 'You stole that, and if I should take any, I would be as bad as any of you for the partaker is as bad as the thief.'" Henry was "a real good fellow." Sutler wrote Frances.
Chancellorsville Campaign begins. Crossed Rappahannock.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcomed letter of April 17th a few days since. Also one the same day from Mary McNeil. I found the Tribune interesting. I'm sorry that you think I did not receive your letters. I assu...
movements.notes: Charles received April 17 letter. Went to Aquia Creek to find whether Alexander came out of fight all right. Got stalling with one of stragglers. **KEY HENRY INTELLIGENCE:** Soldier from Co. D, 34th Regt knew Henry, said he was killed — "he saw the name on a headboard at his grave." Soldier's name is **Abram Fry**, belongs to last N.Y. artillery. He said artillery waited after battle then sessions carried shovels, picks, etc. The man belonging to 34th was hurt at battle of Antietam. In hospital 15 months. "I am afraid he was killed." Scott — thinks he can find more. Troops at the Methodist church — good sermon. "Enclosed is a $40 allotment check."
Battle of Chancellorsville. 60th NY engaged. Jackson's flank attack.

movements.letterExcerpt: I now hasten to write you a few lines to let you know of my welfare. This is my first opportunity of writing you since I left Stevenson. We have been marching hard — very hard for the last few days.
movements.notes: Alexander writes from "Camp somewhere in the State of Georgia" [sic — likely still in Virginia]. Marching hard since leaving Stevenson. Boots from Bridgeport, Ala. sold — too small. "We are close upon the enemy. Our advance came upon them this morning but they fell back." Between 35,000 and 40,000 men under Hooker. Extreme right of the army. Culver Bostwick arrived. Short, urgent. "P.S. Keep a stout heart."

movements.letterExcerpt: I presume you have long ere this heard of the battle of Chancellorsville in which my regiment was employed. I am sorry to say I was not in the battle, being in command of the guard at the Headquarters...
movements.notes: **CHANCELLORSVILLE BATTLE REPORT.** "I presume you have long ere this heard of the battle of Chancellorsville." Alexander's regiment engaged — "I am now relieved from that duty and am again with the reg't." The exact loss: "seventy three — nine killed, forty three wounded, and twenty-one missing. Company H lost six men — one killed dead, Lester Bond." Bond shot through forehead and instantly killed. "The trains were but a short distance from the battle field, and I could distinctly hear every shot and even the cheers of the boys when charging. A heavy body of woods prevented my witnessing the battle." 60th made three charges. Mrs. Hoyle acknowledged.

movements.letterExcerpt: I went to Aquia Creek this morning and on my return this afternoon at about 4:00 P.M. found a letter for me that came this morning after I left. Went to the Creek for two reasons; one of them was that...
movements.notes: Charles went to Aquia Creek to find out about Alexander — went to Aquia Creek. Alex told him he was not in the fight, was detailed to guard baggage train. Charles saw 16 Regt NYV going home. **HENRY — DEFINITIVE:** "As for his Fry, his story is very doubtful and there is no telling where he is now. I think there is not the least doubt that Henry was killed." Regiments going home daily. Some may stay all summer. Lieut. ordered corporal to be drilled for being absent. Bought watch for $12.25, sold for $16.50. Ambrotype enclosed — taken May 11th.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of the 3rd just after we returned from the front and was pleased to hear of your safety. I feared you had been obliged to leave Alexandria as it was reported here that the army ...
movements.notes: Alexander writes to Charles from Aquia Landing. Detailed Chancellorsville account. Company L. Bond killed; G. Ploof wounded; H. Myers wounded; P. Brookway wounded (ditto); I. Stone missing; B. Brame, Orderly Sergeant Brookway missing. Luther uninjured. **April 13th addition:** Couldn't mail — rebels shelling hospitals, ammunition trains. Cavalry captured two rebel guns. May 14th: Rebels commenced shelling again — cavalry charge. "Please let the Capt. know the loss of the company." **May 19 addition (Charles's):** Charles received letter — was "very much gratified yesterday to receive a letter from Alexander." Will buy watch.

movements.letterExcerpt: I was very much gratified yesterday to receive a letter from Alexander. Have been anxiously expecting a letter from either you or him for some time. He has probably written you that he came safely out...
movements.notes: Charles received Alexander's letter — gratified. Will buy watch and send by express. Need $11.20 of Alex's money. Alex told Charles he came safely out of fight, was detailed to guard baggage train. **VISIT TO ALEXANDER AT AQUIA CREEK.** Went on mail steamer, slept on floor, arrived at Aquia Creek. Alex told Charles he was not in the fight. "Our Serg. told him I belonged to his, but they told me I could not pass." Waited nearly two hours then guards let all go. Alex "is well." Alex wants discharge applied for. New law for corporal duty. Burdick is back, promoted to Captain. Another Capt. is now Lt. Col. and Capt. Strain is Major and "the Major is Col."

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter two or three days since containing eleven dollars. Since I last wrote you, I have been to Aquia Creek to see Alex. Found him well and much surprised to see me. The watch that I ...
movements.notes: Charles visited Alexander at Aquia Creek — found him well. Watch: double-cased silver lever, bought from Serg. in Co. for $20, Charles paid $15 cash down. Alex "is well." Alex not in fight — detailed to guard baggage train. Alex told Charles he was not in battle "said he felt bad that he could not be in the fight with his reg't." Serg. told him he could not pass, but guards eventually let go. Burdick back, promoted Captain. Stockades around city — hardwood logs. Cavalry raid expected. 9-months regiment came here. Breastworks not breastworks — stockades. Heavy gates. Sunday night work on stockades. Methodist church — preacher wanted $1.50 to fix church.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcome letter of May (something) today, and am much pleased that you have at length heard from me. Tell me when you next write whether it was my first or second letter you received. I...
movements.notes: Alexander at Aquia Creek Landing. Received letter of May. Pleased Mother has at length heard from him. Heard from Lt. Col. Redington — "very fine man." Describes Col. Redington physically: "about the minimum height, rather slender and very erect." A musician, bargainer — "he is a man of courage." At Chancellorsville he was "singing away at a great rate, using the screams of the shells as they passed over his head as a key to pitch his voice on." **CHAMPLAIN BOYS celebrating with powder — dangerous.** June 4: orders to march with 3 days rations. "It is probably merely a reconnoissance. Luther's father is here."

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcome letter of June 2nd yesterday and was glad to hear from you. Enclosed is a few lines that I received from Alex. Received two more letters from him dated the 7th this morning. He...
movements.notes: Charles received June 2 letter. Enclosed "a few lines" from Alexander. Received two more letters from Alex dated 7th. Alex wrote first because forgot to include ring measurement; second because forgot stamp. "He went to Falmouth. Amos' letter was dated June 8th and says they marched to Falmouth." Fort Lyons magazine exploded yesterday — killing 20 and wounding about same number. Made great noise. Fort is about a mile from city, in sight of regiment's camp. Pay received — $20 check enclosed. Henry's back pay and bounty: "I think that you ought to apply at once for Henry's back pay and bounty." Bought watch for $12.25, sold for $16.50. Had two swims in Potomac this week. Charlotte visit suggested. Welky in tent has History of Rome, France, United States.
Gettysburg Campaign begins. March north through Frederick.
Remained in DC defenses during Gettysburg Campaign.
Remained in DC defenses during Gettysburg Campaign.

movements.letterExcerpt: I have received two papers from you since Mother left home. How do you get along alone and where are you staying? Received a very short letter from Mother a few days since which I answered. Suppose sh...
movements.notes: Charles writes to Frances. Received two papers since Mother left home. Very short letter from Mother. Supposes she is still at Charlotte. **INCOMPLETE — text cut off at bottom of final PDF page.**
Battle of Gettysburg. 60th NY heavily engaged on Culp's Hill / Cemetery Hill.

movements.letterExcerpt: God has again in his great kindness preserved my life through another most terrific battle. I have not received a scratch. The reg't. lost fifty-two — eleven killed and forty-some wounded. We commence...
movements.notes: **GETTYSBURG BATTLE REPORT.** "God has again in his great kindness preserved my life through another most terrific battle." Reg't lost 52 — 11 killed, 41 wounded. Fighting from 2 PM July 2nd through midnight, then nearly all day July 3rd. Milebus Ayres killed, Sgt Brookway and Pvt John Tickle wounded. "We have gained a great victory. We are burying our and the rebel's dead today."
Pursuit of Lee through South Mountain passes.
Extended garrison duty at Capitol Hill barracks and DC defenses.
Extended garrison duty at Capitol Hill barracks and DC defenses.

movements.letterExcerpt: I read a letter from you a few days since and was glad to learn that you were enjoying yourself. Am glad that Grandmother recommended you hope for I run one you are at home by, this time. Think her vi...
movements.notes: Grand parade of all troops on July 4th. Henry's bounty — "suppose you apply late you will have to wait some time for it." Blackberries by the Potomac. Deserter from Co. on furlough caught in Lawrence County, Plattsburgh. Grandmother McNeill and rest at Charlotte. Frances going to Charlotte. Mrs. Brink passing the summer.

movements.letterExcerpt: I wrote you immediately after the battle of Gettysburg (through which I came unscratched) but am somewhat afraid you may never get the letter and accordingly I now write you again to let you know of m...
movements.notes: Gettysburg aftermath. "We beat the rebels gloriously in that battle. The old 60th took two stands of colors from the enemy. We stretched seven rebel officers out in a row in front of the company." 7-8 miles from Antietam battlefield — will visit and try to find out about Henry. "My life is in God's hands. His will be done."
Engagement at Funkstown during pursuit of Lee.
March south to Virginia. Encamped near Warrenton Junction.

movements.letterExcerpt: I have not received a letter since July 8th and I am a little vexed at your long silence. But I try to excuse you by thinking that you and Frances are both busy. I have not written because I have been...
movements.notes: Left Alexandria. Capitol Hill Washington. Capt. Rich left for Champlain to get band of 26th NY for Gen. Slough; also trying to get drafted men from Champlain into their reg't. Steais and Douglas have list from home of big bugs drafted — Sid and Silas lucky to escape, $300 doesn't grow on every bush. General review of troops tomorrow. Marched in hot sun July 4th. Soldiers will be home to vote at election Tuesday. Blackberries — crossed river to Maryland with pass, half bushel of berries.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcome letter of July 16th. Was glad to hear from you and Frances. Rec'd a letter from James dated the 18th. He writes in good spirits. Am glad that Alex came safely out of that Getty...
movements.notes: Left Alexandria — now at Capitol Hill Barracks, Washington D.C. Sudden, unexpected move. Detached from reg't for six months. Ration theft — Jim Lucas and orderly sergeant James Lucas arrested and tried for selling rations. Four of Co. under arrest. $20 check enclosed. Frances did right putting out money. Private in Co. court-martialed for being dirty.

movements.letterExcerpt: I have at length found leisure and materials to write you a few lines. We are now having a few days of rest after our long and painful marching and much we need it. I was nearly worn out when we reach...
movements.notes: Post-Gettysburg rest at Warrenton Junction. Draft excitement. "So Albert Cook and the rest of the 34th are at home, eh!" — scorn for returned soldiers. "Sunny South" is no home for him. P.S.: "I had the satisfaction of firing about fifty or sixty shots into the very teeth of the rebels at Gettysburg." Charged with hoots and yells, stopped them — "it was out of the other corner of their mouths."
At Capitol Hill barracks. Unit preparing for western transfer.

movements.letterExcerpt: It is a long time since I wrote you and the reason is we are all very busy. We are on guard from one to two days at a time. Still I might write while on guard if I could carry the writing materials wi...
movements.notes: Capitol Hill Barracks, Washington. Reg't guards two prisons and R.R. Depot. Draft — examining drafted men and substitutes at city hall. Young citizen caught at depot trying to run from draft. Received letter from Mary McNeill. James Lucas reduced for stealing rations. Capt. Burdick resigned — going home very soon. Whiskey — small quantity given daily. Some kind of medicine.

movements.letterExcerpt: I was very glad to receive a letter from you and James and Frances yesterday. Have been expecting a letter from you for some time. Am glad that you and Frances are both well. My health is good.
movements.notes: Barracks life — prefers barracks to tents: windows, room, bunks. Guard duty: two prisons, R.R. depot, provost marshal. Draft continues — 50 men daily to city hall. Chaplain preaches, experiences meetings. Roaring Methodist in Co. Charlotte visit suggested for Mother and Frances. Break up housekeeping this winter. Frances would like to leave home. Mrs. Boyle — cow, $40 price. Savages — $16.55 debt. Surrogate papers. Sid and wife — big house, won't get rich farming. Jeff nearly played out — guerrilla fighting.

movements.letterExcerpt: I presume you would like to pull my hair right lustily — (rather a difficult matter, by the way, as it is not over an inch or two in length) for not writing you before. I plead guilty and promise all ...
movements.notes: Teasing letter to Frances. "I presume you would like to pull my hair right lustily." "Baltimore widows" — something about Captain Ran. Frances's curiosity. Rappahannock quiet — expect stirring times before many weeks. Mr. Simonds — rod to castigate "young ideas" of Champlain. **ANTIETAM VISIT:** "During the march in Maryland, I passed over a part of the battle ground of Antietam... I longed to leave the ranks and hunt for some trace of Henry, but it was impossible." Sgt. Howes reduced for drunkenness. Amos Luther promoted to his place. $15 sent by express.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of the 20th of August tonight — and feel — Oh! so bad. I do not blame you for writing as you do, but I should like to know the reason why you do not get my letters. Mother, duri...
movements.notes: Deeply emotional letter. "Mother, could you for a moment suppose I could ever forget my old home and my Mother? Never, never." Moved to 2nd Division, 12th Army Corps. Letters lost — "general orders" not to send valuable matter in mail; letters from divisions found by railroad, rifled of contents. Camp near river — pleasant spot, cool water. Picket duty — rebels across river, 100 yards wide. Rebel fired two shots at night pickets, wounding one severely. Rebels exchange newspapers. "The settling of the war was left to the soldiers we would do it in short order. Some of the Rebs are pretty nice fellows."

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcome letter of Aug. 28th in due time. Was very glad to receive so long a letter. I did not know as four weeks had gone by without my writing, but I suppose I was waiting for you to ...
movements.notes: Burdick visited — headache night he left. Letter from James with picture — "looks very well." Frances wants to know about "fair correspondent." Corporal Beardslee wants pictures from Frances — saving money. Methodist church incident — soldier visited whiskey, "the ladies looked blank and turned up their noses." Chaplain used mass rooms. Harpers Magazines and books — small library. 1st Lieut on furlough. Capt. Rich attending to conscripts near Fonda.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received the Tribune two or three days since, and yesterday rec'd. a letter from Alex. He was well and having a pleasant time.
movements.notes: Camp Davis, Capitol Hill. Tribune received, letter from Alex. Demerits at West Point — James. "I think you have the wrong idea about the no. of demerits..." 150 first six months, 100 for second half year; 150 demerits in six months discharges first year. Alex Douglas not very well — in finest, but expects furlough soon. Pet Steais in hospital — chest problem. Boy in Co. who was engaged to girl before enlisting, sent $200 pay/bounty; she spent all money, married, gone to Hell. Talk of leaving — pay today if leaving. Free library in city — soldiers draw books.

movements.letterExcerpt: I have just witnessed the execution of two deserters. They belonged to this Brigade. Every man that was not on duty was obliged to be there. One of the poor fellows was obliged to shoot three times be...
movements.notes: **EXECUTION OF DESERTERS WITNESSED.** "I have just witnessed the execution of two deserters." Every man not on duty obliged to be there. Shot three times. Sat on coffins beside graves. After execution, marched by coffins to "see them and learn a lesson." Five others shot elsewhere same day. **SWORD TO CAPTAIN DELANEY** — Co. H presented sword. Being paid — $15 sent, $20 this time. **ANNIVERSARY OF ANTIETAM** — "Yesterday was the anniversary of the battle of Antietam. I presume I shall be in another battle soon." James' photograph received — "does not look very natural to me." $15 express receipt enclosed.

movements.citation: Dyer's Compendium: 'Movement to Bridgeport, Ala., Sept. 24-Oct. 3'
movements.notes: XI and XII Corps ordered west to reinforce Rosecrans at Chattanooga.

movements.letterExcerpt: I read your welcome letter of Sept. 21 yesterday, also one at the same time from Mary McNeill. By the way, I don't exactly fancy corresponding with a cousin I have never seen. She says the three famil...
movements.notes: Detached 12 men and 2 corporals from Co. — 3 days rations, overcoats, rubber blankets. Going to guard prisoners from here to somewhere. Alex Douglas expects furlough — 20 days. Uncle Sam charges .35 for socks. Two stoves in quarters. Mrs. Brikerhoff will live with Mother this winter. James — demerits, 150 first half, 180 second half. Learned to play checkers. P.S. Detail in morning — two squads leaving, two days rations.

movements.letterExcerpt: I wrote you a few days since, but will write you again to let you know I have seen Alex. He requested me to inform you about him. Last night while our Co. were drawn up to go out on dress parade who s...
movements.notes: **SAW ALEXANDER** — briefly, at night before leaving for duty. Alex looked healthy, moustache sprouting, "not a vine in his mouth." Saw Amos Luther well. **POINT LOOKOUT** — took 282 rebel prisoners from Old Capitol prison on steamer down Potomac and Chesapeake Bay. 3000 prisoners already there. Rebels poorly dressed, ragged — currency depreciated; $160/year for clothing. They don't think much of money, give man for Co. a $10 bill. Said their army all the better for getting rid of bad men. Lieut. Knapp gone to Moorestown on leave. Alex D. no furlough. Capt. Rich brought 1100 conscripts from NY. Uncle John's visit. Jim Lucas — Pet Steais discharge.
Rail transfer through Nashville en route to Chattanooga theater.
Bridgeport/Stevenson area. Preparing for Chattanooga operations.

movements.letterExcerpt: I am highly provoked with you! Here you have excited my curiosity to its highest pitch by telling me that something "very, very funny has happened" — and then wind up by telling me that you "dare not ...
movements.notes: **MURFREESBORO, TENNESSEE** — first letter from Western Theater. "Baltimore widows" teasing continues. Frances received two military novels — "directed on the back to Serg. A. F. Hubbell and then crossed out." Tennessee not much different from rest of world — forts built of cotton bales. First large fields of cotton seen. P.S. Gen. Greene as garrison commander — infantry, cavalry, artillery.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter enclosing Frances' letter of Oct. 4th in due time. Was glad to hear from you both.
movements.notes: Alex may not write soon — unsettled. Church — Chaplain experiences meeting, Roaring Methodist, schools in mess rooms weekly. **COLORED ODD FELLOWS PARADE** — marched through streets in uniforms with gay banners; nigger band; rear brought up with women riding in coaches alongside white women. Policemen watching. Alex Douglas left 6:30 for home — 15 days furlough. Major Strain's wife. War prediction — 2 more years unless foreign interference. Have you sold wool? Wood from Sid's pasture — elm logs.

movements.letterExcerpt: I read a letter from you a few days since, also one yesterday from James, which I will enclose with this. I guess a man at Point Lookout will have to be very economical not to be in debt at the end of...
movements.notes: **CARROLL PRISON — BELLE BOYD** confined there. "She called to see Belle Boyd who is confined there and is a rebel and has a small secesh flag which she shows to the guard." Young lady in broadcloth pants visited prison superintendent — told her women had no business in army. Bought vest $3. 1st Lieut married lady from Alexandria. Co. member went home with discharge — Silas. Man at Point Lookout. Many regts arriving from north going to front. President's new call for men.
Night Battle of Wauhatchie. 60th NY engaged. Secured supply line to Chattanooga.

movements.letterExcerpt: I rec'd the letter and box brought by Alex, who arrived here the 29th. Am very much obliged for all the nice things you sent which were unaccounted. The dried apples though, I don't know exactly what ...
movements.notes: Read letter and box brought by Alex [Douglas]. Dried apples, nice things. Furlough — Lieut asked, declined for now. $1.50 in money, mostly worthless. Cough for about a week. Capt. Rich — visited Alex but missed him. Tribune news is old by time he gets it — 2¢ to send. **POCKET BOOK STOLEN** — $18.78 taken from pocket at dinner; thief returned empty book Sunday evening. Lost all money. Returned old guns, getting new ones. Story about Col. going to Canada.

movements.letterExcerpt: Your letter of Oct. 21st rec'd. yesterday. It was the right thing in the right place for I was feeling particularly lonely. We are now holding a pass in the Cumberland Mountains about fifteen miles be...
movements.notes: **WAUHATCHIE — NIGHT BATTLE.** "We are now holding a pass in the Cumberland Mountains about fifteen miles below Chattanooga." Rebels made furious assault on camp — pickets barely alarmed before enemy was upon them. **GEN. GEORGE S. GREENE WOUNDED** — Brigade commander, seriously if not mortally. **LIEUT. GEARY KILLED** — son of Gen'l Geary, Division commander. Gen. Geary himself slightly wounded in toe. Rebels shelled wagon trains. Pickets fired on cavalry. Discharge — views fully; useless to apply, chief magistrate has power. Anxious to pursue studies. Books — "tell her I know something about them."
Encamped at Wauhatchie. Holding the 'Cracker Line' supply route.

movements.letterExcerpt: I rec'd your letter of Nov. 7th yesterday and was glad to hear from you. Mr. Roberts from C. is here visiting his cousin. He says he is going to Meade's army and is to receive $48 a month in the photo...
movements.notes: Mr. Roberts from C. visiting cousin — going to Meade's army, photograph business, $48/month. Capt. Rich got back — 1,846 rebel prisoners at depot, cavalry took them to Old Capitol prison. Heavy detail to Point Lookout. Those who went home to vote — cheese. Selling house/land. Savages settlement. Uncle John's visit. James near exam — 2 months left, fall short of 100. Goddard's letter — return to James. Jim Lucas — Pet Steais discharge. Frances' letter — short.

movements.letterExcerpt: Have you heard from James and Alex lately? James has owed me a letter for some time, but I suppose he is very busy in the reason. My health is good and I hope that I will stand the winter. But we may ...
movements.notes: Multi-date letter: Nov 20, 21, 23. Not heard from Alex lately. $20 check enclosed (Nov 21). Col. got back — trying to get reg't to Philadelphia but probably Alexandria. Major Strange doesn't like Alexandria. Clothing acct settled — $2.70 due for clothes; some men largely in debt. **POCKET BOOK STOLEN** — $18.78 taken; money was in it when found Saturday; returned Sunday evening empty. Person who found it first took money. Returned old guns, getting new ones — good guns. Col. may go to Canada — five of Co. on furlough.

movements.letterExcerpt: So you defy me, eh! I believe I put a flea in your ear in the last letter I wrote home. Didn't I now! Don't you wish you knew who sent those books? I know, but I'll be bound if I'll tell. How did you ...
movements.notes: "Harry Lorrequer" (Lever novel) and "Maud the Knight of Dettine" — books discussion. Ordered to fall in with knapsacks — marched to Division headquarters and back. Gen. Geary — "a dry joke, considering the rain and mud." Professor Bass flourishing. Capt. Delaney — letter from Capt. Ransom asking to use influence for Alexander's discharge. Mother seems averse to giving up the idea. Secretary Stanton is the man to apply to, or else the President. 11 months to serve. Frances — send shirts, socks, boots by express to Nashville, Tenn.

movements.citation: Dyer's Compendium: 'Battle of Lookout Mountain Nov. 24'
movements.notes: Battle of Lookout Mountain — 'Battle Above the Clouds'.

movements.citation: Dyer's Compendium: 'Battle of Missionary Ridge Nov. 25'
movements.notes: Battle of Missionary Ridge. Dramatic uphill assault.
Battle of Ringgold Gap. Pursuit of Bragg after Missionary Ridge.

movements.letterExcerpt: I presume you will be surprised to hear from me from this place. Well here I am in the hospital. I was wounded at the storming of Lookout Mountain. I am not seriously hurt. I am wounded in my left sid...
movements.notes: **WOUNDED AT LOOKOUT MOUNTAIN.** "I presume you will be surprised to hear from me from this place. Well here I am in the hospital." Wounded at the storming of Lookout Mountain — minie ball in left side. "Rather a close call for my life, I think." Not seriously hurt; expects to rejoin regiment soon. **CASUALTIES:** George Hays killed; Sergts Hubbell and Long, Corporals Ish and Kelly, Private Sidney Rider wounded; Majo, Doten, Housedean killed. Thomas Small had his leg torn off. "The rebs ran like good fellows." Took whole posse (1,800) prisoner.
Winter camp at Wauhatchie / Tullahoma area.

movements.letterExcerpt: There are no more signs of our leaving this place than the day we were relieved from duty. We on duty but are waiting for marching orders. Some think that we will stay here all winter. Others say that...
movements.notes: No signs of leaving Capitol Hill. Camp fire, barracks being built. Half rations — "the whole army is in the same way." Railroad will bring abundance soon. **CO. H LOSSES AT LOOKOUT MOUNTAIN** — per Charles: "Doten and Michael Housedean, killed; Alfred Lemage and Thomas Small, wounded. Thos. Small had his leg torn off." Old Bragg well used up. Missionary Ridge and Ringgold. Half rations. **INCOMPLETE — text cuts off.**

movements.letterExcerpt: Our Regt. commenced doing duty this morning again. We now guard Carrol Prison again, relieving the Invalid Corps from that duty. We all now expect to stay here this winter, because we are doing duty a...
movements.notes: Reg't commenced doing duty again — guarding Carroll Prison, relieving Invalid Corps. Expect to stay here this winter. Alexandria visit — Gen. Slough's headquarters. Near barracks. Good many white shirts, collars — $5 each. Theaters attended by officers — pass till 12 PM. Chaplain formed union church — all denominations. Sacrament administered at Methodist. Last Sunday — full communion. Checkers. Have you heard from Alex? "I am anxious to hear from him, but I don't borrow trouble."

movements.letterExcerpt: I presume you have about come to the conclusion that I have left the land of the living or else entirely forgotten you, but it is no such thing. I have not forgotten you, though I would not blame you ...
movements.notes: **DETAILED BATTLE NARRATIVE — LOOKOUT MOUNTAIN, MISSIONARY RIDGE, RINGGOLD.** "We were often required to halt ourselves on with our hands, which you know, in the face of the enemy is not over pleasant." 60th has been in THREE fights since Wauhatchie. Division chosen to storm Lookout Mountain. Nashville and Chattanooga railroad. Five regiments fought Longstreet night of Oct 28th — Whiteside. Three regts of brigade engaged. Gen'l Greene wounded. **WOUNDED BY BALL IN SIDE** — "stretched me out in short order." **LOSSES:** Lemage, Tees, Rider, Small, Hubbell wounded; Majo, Doten, Housedean killed. Thomas Small had leg torn off. "Do not write until you hear from me again as we expect to make a move soon."

movements.letterExcerpt: I am again with the regt. and doing duty. My side is still pretty sore but then I manage to get along first rate. My wound caused me to miss the fights of Missionary Ridge and Ringgold. I did not like...
movements.notes: Side still sore but doing duty. Left hospital — told surgeon he was ready, returned to regt. Two others came back with him. Back in old camp. Half rations — "pretty hard up for rations." **CO. H LOSSES — FINAL LIST:** "Doten and Michael Housedean, killed; Alfred Lemage and Thomas Small, wounded. Thos. Small had his leg torn off." P.S. Sergt. Long was not hurt. Old Bragg will be wiped out before long. Railroad will open in a few days — abundance soon. "Do not write until you hear from me again as we expect to make a move soon." Only a small bit of candle left.

movements.letterExcerpt: I wish you and Frances a happy New Year. Did either of you pass a pleasant New Year's day? I was on guard but passed it well enough. On that day we had boiled flour pudding for supper. It was new busi...
movements.notes: New Year's Day — on guard. Flour pudding for supper; 2 kegs of lager beer $5.50; baked bread pudding with raisins. Christmas morning an Irishman found drunk at roadside — "he was having his Christmas." Old regts re-enlisting — 30 days furlough and large bounty. 14th New Hampshire received marching orders countermanded. "Hardsburger" or Harper's Ferry. Stealing in regt — turkeys, chickens. Soldier court-martialed for being dirty. Geo. Dodds came from hospital to see Champlainers.

movements.letterExcerpt: I know you think I am a very naughty boy not to write you oftener, but as I have said before, it is hard for me to write when I get no answers to my letters. This state of things I trust will not last...
movements.notes: **RE-ENLISTED AND LEFT CHATTANOOGA CLANDESTINELY.** Alexander left detachment to rejoin regiment. "I suppose I am reported at my detachment as a deserter, but this will do me no harm as I shall be able to join the regt. before my report can reach there." Smuggled way with 18th Corps detachment to Nashville. On way to Savannah to join regt. Col. Strain arranged reassignment. Shall go by way of New York — medical examination. "I shall come home, probably, unless I should fail to pass the medical examination at New York."

movements.letterExcerpt: I rec'd. your welcome letter of Jan. 11th a few days since and would have answered it before but I have been on guard and we have had general inspection. Am sorry that Alex has reenlisted, but it may ...
movements.notes: Alex has re-enlisted. **COL. AND ADJUTANT UNDER ARREST.** Lieut. Col. Armstrong, ex-Col., also Lieut. Col. Prentoff, ex-quartermaster. Charges against Col. — incompetency. He has preferred charges against our Col. in revenge. Corporal Trombly — passed examining board, 2nd Lieut. in colored regt. **BUCKING AND GAGGING DESCRIBED** — stick in mouth tied with string, hands fastened at wrist, placed under knees. "Niggers are punished in this way in the South." Lafountain — brother in Co. did not re-enlist; injured on Ogdensburg railroad. Alex's letters directed same; Alex will write soon. Mary McNeill — letter owed.

movements.letterExcerpt: I rec'd. your welcome and long looked for letter of Jan. 20 yesterday. Am glad to hear that Alex is enjoying his furlough. Hope that he will continue to have a good time. But I hope that he won't negl...
movements.notes: Alex enjoying furlough — hopes he improves penmanship. $450 town bounty discussion — quota may not be full. Savages settlement — $16.56. County bonds at 7% preferred over investment. Chas. Carte visited — saw Champlainers at Biglows. James's abilities — "a great many smart men have failed at West Point." Sid having trouble in family. Love feast — soldier said he felt love of God. Guard bribed $200 to let prisoner escape. **ATTENDED CONGRESS** — debate between Democrat and Republican.

movements.letterExcerpt: I rec'd. Alex's letter of Feb. 9th enclosing one dollar two or three days since. Have been on guard or would have answered it sooner. Since the 14th N.H. regt. left for the front two or three weeks si...
movements.notes: **TRANSFERRED TO POINT LOOKOUT.** Guard duty at prisoner camp — nearly 400 rebel prisoners, ~8,000 total. Board fence with walk near top for sentinels. Old Capitol Prison and Carroll Prison also guarded. Four reliefs instead of three — on duty all the time. Jim Lucas promoted again to Corporal. Regt left front two or three weeks ago — doing duty for 14th N.H. too. Alex's bounty — town bounty question. Sam Underhill not entitled.
Brief stop at Point Lookout (POW camp) during transfer south.

movements.letterExcerpt: Military movements are sudden so you must not be surprised to hear that we are to leave this place tomorrow morning at 7 o'clock for Alexandria. It was un-expected, our being relieved from duty last n...
movements.notes: **SUDDEN MARCHING ORDERS — LEAVING FOR ALEXANDRIA.** "Military movements are sudden." Leave tomorrow 7 o'clock for Alexandria. Received 2 months pay. Col. has returned — "men cheered him roundly." Some think going to Texas or Army of the Potomac. Sold large double-cased watch for $17.50. Coldest day of winter. Encloses $20 check and $10.60 in greenbacks. Alex's photograph looks well.

movements.letterExcerpt: I wrote you a day or two at on from Louisville, Ky., but you recollect I promised to write you as often as possible — and as I have plenty of leisure at present, I don't know as I can better occupy it...
movements.notes: Left Louisville yesterday morning — reached Nashville before dark. **THOS. SMALL VISITED AT HOSPITAL** — lost his leg at Ringgold; doing well, cheerful. Luther spent greater part of state bounty — Marshall Dunn said state bounty yet; $5 reward for services. Direct letters to Nashville, Army of the Cumberland. Boys from Champlain all well. Frances and school — Mrs. Rider, Miss Riley, Miss Averill.
Returned to Stevenson/Bridgeport area. Preparing for Atlanta Campaign.

movements.letterExcerpt: It is a most beautiful Sabbath morning. The sun is shining warm and pleasant, the birds are singing, and every thing is hushed to an unusual quiet. It is such a day as is seldom vouchsafed to us soldi...
movements.notes: **SOLDIER'S HOME AT STEPHENSON, ALA.** Beautiful Sabbath morning — birds singing. "Horse thief" Morgan on the move — 8,000 men. All troops under arms last night. **VETERANS OF 64** — reached here night before last. Soldier's Home — excellent supper, good sleeping accommodations. Tent mates: Corporal Kelly, Oliver Lafountain, George Bully. Opposite camp — soldiers buried, victims of Chickamauga; General Hospital. **REBEL CAPTAIN CONVERSATION** — "they send a whole regt. of cavalry to guard half a dozen conscripts." Johnson's (Bragg's) army swear they won't stand in next battle. Gen'l Slocum speech — speedy termination of war. "The Old Sixtieth" paper from Christian Com. Brigade Band serenade.

movements.letterExcerpt: We reached this place yesterday afternoon after a march of some sixty miles. I have not yet been around to see the lions of the place; but shall as soon as possible. The Johnnies must have left here i...
movements.notes: Reached Charleston, S.C. (likely Charleston, Tenn.) after march of 60 miles. Johnnies left in haste — guns left unmuzzled, carriages burned, two enormous rifled guns on track. "I expect Kilpatrick slipped them us on that calculation by tearing up the railroads." Immense ordnance left. Sherman off again — no telling when they'll get to him. Transports from this place likely. Remember me to Mrs. B.

movements.letterExcerpt: Here we are just across the river close to New Orleans. We left Washington Feb. 18th for Alexandria and stayed there in the Soldier's Rest till the 20th when we went aboard the steamship Mississippi b...
movements.notes: **LEFT WASHINGTON FOR NEW ORLEANS.** Left Washington Feb. 18 for Alexandria, stayed at Soldier's Rest till 20th, steamship Mississippi to N.O. Reached N.O. about sundown Feb. 28. Passed pleasant Sabbath on deck looking at sugar plantations. **"ALGIERS"** — across river from New Orleans. Quartered in iron works — brick building, no floor, windows nearly all smashed. Expedition fitting out for Mobile or Texas. Sleeping in bunks 4-5 in a bunk. Hardtack and mess, coffee boiled in iron tank by steam. Oranges 6¢ each, apples 10¢. Darkies threw oranges at boat.
With 153rd NY in Louisiana. Red River Campaign area.

movements.letterExcerpt: I came to this place March 3d, which is Gen'l. Banks Head Quarters. On the afternoon of the 2nd the Col sent for me and asked whether I would like to go to N. Orleans as clerk. After looking at my han...
movements.notes: **CLERK AT GEN. BANKS HEADQUARTERS.** Came to New Orleans March 3rd — Col. Strain sent for him, asked if he'd like to go to N.O. as clerk. After looking at handwriting, Capt. would give consent. Col. Strain — "a very pleasant man and you must thank Mrs. Strain for her influence." 3rd story, fresh cool air. **REGIMENT LEFT FOR FRANKLIN, LA.** — expects hard marching. 153rd going to Texas, he believes. Extra pay 40¢/day — $25/month total. **FREE STATE GOVERNOR INAUGURATED** — 5,000 school children, cannon firing, musketry, fireworks. Streets flooded with rain. Bad spelling acknowledged — "wish you would correct my bad spelling."
Stationed at New Orleans. Preparing for Red River Campaign support.

movements.letterExcerpt: I rec'd. your welcome letters of Feb. 14th, 18th, and 22rd and also one enclosed from Frances yesterday. Am sorry to hear that Charley has left Wash. Had hoped he would remain there all summer. I hope...
movements.notes: Sorry Charley has left Washington — hoped he'd stay all summer. **REBEL DESERTERS FROM LONGSTREET'S AND JOHNSON'S ARMY** — "give a most dolorous acc't of the affairs of the so-called Southern Confederacy." Johnson's army suffering terribly for food — one day's rations scarcely sufficient for one meal. Determined not to stand in next fight. "Said the Confederacy was played out and that it was only the pride of the leaders that kept it up." Longstreet's men also doleful. 62d Corps very well acquainted — asked us if we had not rather be in "the Potomac army." **AVERILL — BOUNTY AND COUNTY BUSINESS.** Marshall Dunn — pay $5 for his fee. County Clerk. Mrs. Bostwick — dolorous times.

movements.letterExcerpt: So you think I know you would give a thousand worlds to see me — eh? You would like to make me think I am something great, wouldn't you? A fine idea, isn't it? How do you know but what I would get so ...
movements.notes: Playful letter to Frances. "You would like to make me think I am something great, wouldn't you?" Warns against flattery — "a certain ancient philosopher who always walked with his head among the stars, might fall into a ditch." Hopes to walk among friends again "in the meek garb of a citizen." "It will be the proudest day of my life." Promises when that time comes will reverse the order — draw Frances on sled to houses. Miss Averill lost sled rides. Brigade Band practicing. History of the Regt. — have you received?

movements.letterExcerpt: Here at last is the long expected letter which I have promised so often. Everything has gone on about as usual since I last wrote. We have got our shanty up and a fireplace built and are now quite com...
movements.notes: **THE LONG-PROMISED LETTER TO FRANCES.** Beautiful day — whole country dotted with camps. Columns of smoke from picket fires. Stars and stripes floating from HQ. Brigade band playing, instruments gleaming. **VIVID CAMP SCENE PAINTING** — drums, bugles, dinner call, tin cup and plate, cook house. "Last but not least — Taps." "Yankee dough face" — Southern women despise Northerners who admire them. Mrs. Bass says three Northern men could be beat before one Southern one could. 30¢/day rations. Marshall Dunn — bounty. Culver Bostwick will come along soon — Elmira. Nathaniel Nichols. Morgan's movements — several little starts.
Red River Campaign. Advanced from Franklin to Alexandria.
Red River Campaign. Advanced from Franklin to Alexandria.

movements.letterExcerpt: I have anxiously been expecting a letter for some time, but as yet have rec'd none. Should like to hear about the boys and how you and Frances get along. But I suppose that I will get one after a whil...
movements.notes: Still at HQ but may not remain much longer. Writing stiff — "they tell me my writing is stiff." No detail from HQ yet. Duty — copying special orders, new copy for smallest mistake. **RED RIVER CAMPAIGN NEWS** — Army has had two or three victories on Red River in western Louisiana. Captured Fort DeRussy, town of Alexandria, taken many prisoners. On its way to Texas. **CAPT. FOX DISMISSED** — disloyalty, conduct unbecoming officer and gentleman. **WOMAN KILLED BY STREET CAR** — poor white woman. "Crescent City" — built on bend in river. "Wicked city" — two or three theatres. Weather cold — "niggers say it is because the whole North has come down here." Picayune — 5¢, smallest change. James enlisted?

movements.letterExcerpt: Have had old warrant renewed so that I now hold my old position in the 60th Veterans. It is merely a matter of form. Please preserve this one as you have the other. It is now some time since I heard f...
movements.notes: Old warrant renewed — holds old position in 60th Veterans. Merely a matter of form. Received marching orders — leaving in few days for Chattanooga or Knoxville, probably. Very much disappointed — no letter. Asks for boots — send in care of Capt. Delaney. Send stamps. Have you heard from James and Charles?

movements.letterExcerpt: Although I have rec'd no letter for so long a time, I think I ought to write once in a while as I have been doing. I think the fault must be in the mail. Today I am to receive over $11.00 extra pay. I...
movements.notes: Still at HQ — no letter for long time. No detail yet from HQ. Extra pay 40¢/day — $25/mo. **GEN. BANKS AND STAFF IN THE FIELD** — Red River. Some clerks with them. "I always go to bed first." Office is his home — keeps knapsack in corner, spreads blankets on floor. Marble mantle, marble washstand with spigot of water. 3rd story. Roses and flowers in bloom — "about a week for the mail to reach the north." **RED RIVER CAMPAIGN** — troops doing very well, expect to clear rebels out of western Louisiana and Texas before long. Wonder if James has enlisted.

movements.letterExcerpt: The last letter I rec'd. from home was dated March 14th. I have, I believe rec'd two papers from home since then. I am feeling very anxious about you all. Where is Charles and have you heard from Jame...
movements.notes: Under marching orders — everything prepared for coming campaign. "May God be with us!" **20TH ARMY CORPS FORMED** — 11th & 12th Army Corps consolidated under Gen. Hooker. Gen. Slocum assigned to command of Vicksburg. "Shall probably have a hard summer. General Hooker never cusses his men. I hope we shall be able to give the rebels a finishing blow this summer." Mrs. Hoyle sending papers. Soldiers voting in Champlain — Mr. Bass cast a vote against. Picket duty relieved — done by other regts now. Surplus baggage to rear — sent overcoat. 6 P.M. — mail came, no letter — "very much disappointed... I fear all is not right at home."

movements.letterExcerpt: It has been a beautiful warm day. The weather of last month was raw and chilly most of the time. If it was a sample of what you had up there, there must have been very little sugar made during the mon...
movements.notes: **10-PAGE LETTER — ONLY 2 PAGES SURVIVE.** **BASEBALL REFERENCE** — "Union Base" game; two regts challenged 60th NY, "our regiment beat them badly." Grand dance on company street — fiddle. Culver Bostwick not yet appeared. Reinforcing Lee prevented — "harass the enemy." April 8th P.S. — horse race, sack race, wheelbarrow race, foot race, cook fight, greased pole. **GREASED PIG.** Shell barrow races — sack over heads. Contrabands run after greased pig. **CONTRABAND PREACHER** — "Fess my brederin, day drove a ten penny nail troo his hands and feet — just as true as you are born!" Magazine received — "Prospects of S.P. Hubbell." Mrs. Reams (Cousin Nell) letter — announcing marriage.

movements.letterExcerpt: Have rec'd no letter yet, but expect one on the steamer due today. I don't know what to think of your long silence. Am afraid sometimes that you are sick, but hope that is not the reason. One week sin...
movements.notes: Saw Sergt. Peltier — was on furlough, joined regt, left North, on way back to join. **TERRIBLE FIGHTING IN WESTERN LOUISIANA** — "called a victory for us but so bloody that we were not able to take advantage of it." Heavy loss on both sides. 153rd was in it. **CLERK KILLED BY FALL** — drunk, spread mattress on office floor, went onto gallery on 3rd story, pitched head first over banister striking stone pavement in yard. "He never saved nor groaned." Sanitary Commission tableau — Mrs. Banks as president. Clerks expect commutation of rations — $60/month including everything. Not heard from home since early February. Penmanship only trouble — "I had rather not write than till I hear from him or home."

movements.letterExcerpt: I rec'd. your letter of the 4th inst. last evening. I was amazed and vexed at your notion (Bonnett call it anything else) of James. He could not have enlisted, been sent to his reg't., drawn his arms,...
movements.notes: **JAMES HAS ENLISTED** — "I very much doubt his enlisting in the cavalry." Thinks James has good chances for commission — Gov. Seymour rather slim. James will be favorite with men — "used to treat us well when we were little shavers." Doubts militia — "abolished." $500 bounty — "if I should ever come home again I should like at least a thousand dollars to start on." Send boots — $90/month pay. Mrs. B. going to live in old Stone Castle. **GEN. THOMAS AND HOOKER VISITED** — Thomas "a tremendous large man," beard snow white. Hooker "as fine a looking officer as you could wish to see." **BASEBALL AGAIN** — 78th N.Y. Vet. Vol. challenged to Union Base game; Alexander participated in grand dance. Kilpatrick's raid — "the Conclusions." Six new regts from Indiana — "marched from Nashville and looked as if they had passed through a campaign — being poor and haggard."

movements.letterExcerpt: We are at length fully organized and now form the 20th Army Corps, Army of the Cumberland. Direct your letters to 3d Brigade, 2nd Div., 20th Army Corps, Army of the Cumberland.
movements.notes: **20TH ARMY CORPS FULLY ORGANIZED.** Direct letters to 3d Brigade, 2nd Div., 20th Army Corps, Army of the Cumberland. 3rd Brigade: 60th, 78th, 102d NY Vets, 29th and 111th Penn. Vets, 137th and 149th NY Volunteers. Corps divided into 4 divisions — same Div. commander, Gen. John M. Geary. **RUMOR: McCLELLAN TO COMMAND ARMY OF THE POTOMAC.** "I have tried hard to forget McClellan... My heart still yearns toward the man. I have never had, and am afraid never can have, the confidence in any military officer that I had in him." Gen. Hooker commands Corps. Wonderfully pleased about boots. Rec'd Aunt Laura's letter, Charles's letters.

movements.letterExcerpt: I was relieved of duty here by Special Order April 21st and ordered to rejoin my Regt at once, but am still here waiting for the boat. I expect to carry the mail to Gen. Banks Hd. Qtrs. in the field, ...
movements.notes: **RELIEVED FROM HQ — ORDERED TO REJOIN REGIMENT.** Special Order April 21st. Expects to carry mail to Gen. Banks Hd. Qtrs. in the field on Red River. State room and subsistence on boat. Army amassed on Red River — will not have far to march to regt. **OVERCOAT AND DRESS COAT LEFT IN N.O.** — carries knapsack, rubber and woolen blankets, half shelter tent. Rec'd letter from Alex — well at Stevenson, under marching orders. **RED RIVER EXPECTS ANOTHER FIGHT.** Two other clerks also relieved. Alex's letter — "I was beginning to think something was the matter" — didn't know where James was. **CONSTITUTIONAL CONVENTION IN SESSION** — French and negroes speak French; debate on publishing laws in English only. **NEW ORLEANS DESCRIBED** — cisterns made of wood above ground, sidewalks called banquettes, street cars drawn by mules, no conductor. Cemeteries — people buried above ground in tombs or in wall. "Some very fine residences in suburbs." **DRY TORTUGAS** — Island of Tortugas great prison for soldiers; fort being built with hard labor. Chief clerk $4/day, interpreters French and German $100/month. Apr. 24 — leaves today or tomorrow. Two letters — one from Alex. Sid's wife and mother should get along. Give regards to Silas and Sid, also David Savage.

movements.letterExcerpt: I rec'd your letter of Apr. 10th yesterday and was very glad to hear from you. Have been waiting to hear from you before I wrote, so that I could have your direction. It is a very long direction. Woul...
movements.notes: Relieved from HQ — waiting for boat. Carrying mail to Banks Hd. Qtrs. in field on Red River. Will ride all the way. Penmanship not good enough. **CLERK KILLED — EXPANDED ACCOUNT.** Drunk, 3rd story gallery, pitched over banister, head on stone pavement. "He never moved." Lot of us gathered around, in drawers and shirts. Buried by the hospitals — 8 bodies from hospital in wagon, corporal and 8 men drove into cemetery. Chaplain couldn't be there — one of the clerks made a prayer, volleys fired, got into street car and came home. **GREAT FIGHT NEAR R. RIVER** — lost great many men. Another battle expected soon. Army amassed on Red River at Grand Encore (Ecore). Dry Tortugas — fort, hard labor, 5-10 years. Street cars by mule, no conductor. Have you heard from James?
Stationed at Alexandria during army's retreat preparations.
Stationed at Alexandria during army's retreat preparations.

movements.letterExcerpt: We leave here in a day or two — perhaps tomorrow — for the front. The eastern troops in this Department have too good a name for bold unflinching bravery to allow them to lie still while the rest of t...
movements.notes: **LEAVING FOR THE FRONT — PERHAPS TOMORROW.** "The eastern troops in this Department have too good a name for bold unflinching bravery to allow them to lie still while the rest of the Army is fighting." Battles probably in a few weeks — "not be a whit behind, and perhaps throw completely in the shade the battles of Antietam and Gettysburg." **"MAY GOD BE WITH US AND GRANT VICTORY TO OUR ARMS."** "I hope the people at the North will keep a stout heart... It is the death struggle of this mighty rebellion." "Our Father in Heaven is watching over us all." Hopes to "come safely out of the struggle — if not, I trust that we shall all meet in the better world." Rec'd letter of 18th — several little matters interspersed delayed answering. Enclosed newspaper clip from Louisville paper — "you may know our Div. and Div. Commander are up." Bridgeport 9 miles from here — HQ of Div.
Atlanta Campaign begins. Advance from Ringgold toward Dalton.

movements.letterExcerpt: I arrived here yesterday and am now back with the regt. Went on board of a steamer, Monday, April 25th at N. Orleans, but after staying some time on her she was ordered not to leave so I went on board...
movements.notes: **ARRIVED AT ALEXANDRIA, LA. — BACK WITH REGIMENT.** Boarded steamer April 25 in N.O. Carried despatches for Gen. Banks. State room with two mail carriers. Soldiers on boat drew rations and cooked themselves. Stopped at Port Hudson — slow boat. **GUERRILLAS FIRED ON STEAMER.** One beef was shot and dragged on board — three soldiers chased cattle into woods, didn't come back. "It is supposed they were shot or taken prisoners by the guerrillas." Passed Fort DeRussy. Next morning — transport with cannon, gunboat in rear. **FIGHT 35 MILES FROM ALEXANDRIA** — one man shot dead, one wounded on boat. Rebs had one cannon — gunboat soon dismantled it. "As I had my gun I fired it into the woods." Three bullets came near where he was. Found 4 letters at regt. Alex Douglass sent 3 to N.O. — didn't receive. Regt. came out on foraging expedition — "never saw such looking men." Dust half inch thick. Writing on ground — "you must excuse the penmanship."

movements.letterExcerpt: I now hasten to write you a few lines to let you know of my welfare. This is my first opportunity of writing you since I left Stevenson. We have been marching hard — very hard for the last few days.
movements.notes: **ATLANTA CAMPAIGN BEGINS.** "Camp somewhere in the State of Georgia." First opportunity to write since leaving Stevenson. Marching hard — "very hard for the last few days." Boots too small — sold to Lafountain for $6.50, now has excellent pair of Govt. bootees. Sugar was excellent. Stripes very nice. **CLOSE UPON THE ENEMY.** Advance came upon them this morning but they fell back. 35,000-40,000 men under Hooker — extreme right of the army. **CULVER BOSTWICK IS HERE** — reached regt. yesterday, drawn new gun, too busy cleaning it. "Keep a stout heart."

movements.citation: Dyer's Compendium: 'Demonstration on Rocky Face Ridge May 8-11'
movements.notes: Demonstration on Rocky Face Ridge / Buzzard Roost Gap.

movements.letterExcerpt: The mail leaves in a few minutes, and I must hasten and have my say for I know you are anxious to hear from your boys in these perilous times. Well, I am happy to say that I am still all right and tru...
movements.notes: Camp near Altoona Creek, Ga. "I am still all right." Culver Bostwick "sends much love to his friends." **SHARPSHOOTING QUALITIES** tested against rebs "with what success I am unable to say." "Movements of the army I am unable to inform you. They are so continued I cannot make heads or tails of them." No word from home since leaving Bridgeport. Heard from James — "he was in that terrible fighting in Va." (Battle of the Wilderness). "It is a great comfort to me, Mother, to know that there is One above who knows all things and does all things for the best. It is such a relief to have One to whom we can go and confide all our griefs and trials." Soldier needs God's help. "With God's help we hope to crush this rebellion this summer." Luther well. Only 2 men of Co. H injured.

movements.letterExcerpt: I wrote you a few days since but will not write you again that you may not be over anxious about me in these perilous times. The 1st & 2nd brigades of our Div. were engaged with the enemy at this plac...
movements.notes: **BATTLE OF BUZZARD'S ROOST (MILL CREEK GAP / ROCKY FACE RIDGE).** 1st & 2nd Brigades engaged at this place Sunday. 3rd Brigade (60th NY) sent out as support to Div. of Cavalry on reconnaissance — did not join Div., firing just ceased when they came up. Buzzard's Roost — "high rocky ridge... accessible by a narrow gap through the high rocky ledge with which its sides are covered." Rebs drove rebels to crest of hill — "they came upon them in great force posted behind rocks and trees and in the ledges from which they fired upon our men such a withering fire that they were obliged to halt, but managed to hold their ground until all our wounded were removed." Believe left dead — "fell back to original position." 3rd Div. of Corps made similar attempt with like effect — "both attacks were but feints to attract the attention of the enemy from other portions of the army." Large force in rear of enemy. "I think the Johnnies will have to 'up and git.'" Heavy cannonade on left this afternoon. Working all last night building breastworks — "the enemy might make a break this way." Dispatch from Army of the Potomac — "had thrashed the rebs and driven them ten miles." Sherman added "let us do likewise."
Battle of Resaca.
Advance through Adairsville to Kingston.
