movements.letterExcerpt: Camp South of the Oostanaula River
movements.notes: **CAME OUT OF BATTLE SUNDAY THE 15TH UNSCATHED.** "I thank God that I am able to inform you that I came out of the battle on Sunday the 15th inst. unscathed." Enemy defeated — now in close pursuit. Loss of army comparatively small. "The troops in this fight went in in a way that I never saw before being formed in solid column." **HEAVY FIRE FROM 11 A.M. TO LONG AFTER DARK.** Due to nature of ground (succession of ridges) loss very slight. "Not a man of Co. H was hurt." Dislikes "much spinning yarns on paper" — will wait to tell in person. **CORRECTION:** Last letter said Buzzard's Roost — should be Mills Ridge (the Ridge is called Mills Ridge). Camp south of Oostanaula River.
Retreat from Alexandria to Morganza. Campaign ends May 22.
Retreat from Alexandria to Morganza. Campaign ends May 22.

movements.letterExcerpt: "At length," I can hear you say, "at length he has found time to write me a letter. Right then, indeed he should, I should think. Not a word has he written since he left on furlough." Now, Miss Fannie...
movements.notes: Camp near Kingston, Ga. "At length he has found time to write me a letter. Right then, indeed he should, I should think." Not a word since left on furlough. "Haven't I nursed a right? I will plead guilty to all charges and beg ten thousand pardons." **LATE BATTLE — Mr. Bass shot and probably fatally.** "I think Dodds must have been deranged. Who will now teach the old Academy? Nor Mrs. Bass!" Two men shot through right lung to liver — doesn't recollect one surviving. Mr. Bass will have advantage that "poor fellows do not have out here — good nursing and the best medical treatment." **REBEL FLAG INCIDENT** — "one of our men the other day, a brutal fellow, when we were casting over the battle field picked up a rebel leg and foot and shook it in our faces with some disgusting remark. I wanted to knock the fellow down with the butt of my gun." Culver Bostwick — "bully soldier. Takes a battle very philosophically and stands the marches first rate." Said he thought "they came out in an open field and fought it out. The late battle ground was a perfect wilderness." Letter from Charles — he was awaiting boat to join regt.

movements.letterExcerpt: Camp on the Bank of the Miss. River
movements.notes: **JAMES ARRIVES AT CAMP!** "I was much surprised yesterday to see James walking into my tent." Came from N. Orleans on transport. Enlisted in N.Y. for this regt. Camp of Distribution about a week. James has not shaved since he left West Point — has quite a pair of whiskers. Looks well and healthy. Says he knew he was going to enlist "because he told Alex." **REJOINED ARMY** after long march from Red River. Left Alexandria, La. — march from Red River "which I think I could never have stood." Ambulances full of sick. Fell out within 2 miles of camp — "I fell out and took my own time." Marched in line of battle to meet rebs — cavalry skirmishing in front — rebs skedaddled. Transports on river to move from here. Passed parts of letters the rebs captured. Alex Douglass is commissary sergt. — $21/month. Rumors of terrible fighting up north — "large loss of life on both sides, but that we were victorious." Col. told regt. Richmond was taken — "he believed it to be authentic." Gave some lusty cheering. Took swim in river — "felt a good deal better after it." Alex Douglas told something about Sid — "either someone was dead, or something burned up."
Garrison duty at Morganza Bend on the Mississippi River.

movements.notes: Battle of New Hope Church / Dallas / Pickett's Mill.

movements.letterExcerpt: I am happy to inform you that I am all right thus far. God has been very good to me. This is written while we are under fire, the bullets whistling over our heads (there goes one now — b-e-a-u-t-i-f-u...
movements.notes: **WRITING UNDER FIRE.** Entrenchments near Dallas, Ga. "This is written while we are under fire, the bullets whistling over our heads (there goes one now — b-e-a-u-t-i-f-u-l) every now and then — not a little oftener." **JAMES THURBER AND JOHN RAWLINS OF CO. H WOUNDED.** Thurber — through arm, slightly in shoulder; Rawlins — right side, not dangerous. Total loss of regt in this big fight: 28 — 7 killed, remainder wounded. Rebel works very close — "we can hear them talk quite frequently and distinctly." Gen'l won't allow them out on skirmish line — "says I am always ready to do my duty — but that is no place for me, — the men of the keenest sight are the only ones that are needed there." Lost silk handkerchief — "almost impossible to get along without one here." Not rec'd letter since leaving Bridgeport.

movements.letterExcerpt: Have just heard that a steamer leaves in a short time for New Orleans so will write you a few lines. As I have to get ready for inspection I cannot write much. This morning I had the pleasure of recei...
movements.notes: Camp on Bank of Mississippi River, Morganza Bend, La. Steamer leaves in short time for N.O. Received letter from Mother dated May 7th, also 2 newspapers and 4 letters directed to Hd. Qtrs. (April 12, 20, 26, May 5). Framework over tents with bushes — shady and cool. Shelter from sun made for horses same way. Will stay in camp till cool weather. Each man does own cooking — draws rations raw. Instead of hard tack, drew flour — made pancakes, fried cakes in frying pan. **JAMES IS LANCE CORPORAL** — "acts as corporal." Has to drill with recruits — doesn't know how long. Has his bounty — will send home when he can find express agent. Trunk gave away — was in Albany hotel 2 weeks, paid $3/day for board. Gave occupation as "farmer." **REC'D $860 BOUNTY** — told would receive $975 at his regt. Not entitled to Clinton Co. bounty — "I think it would be well to inquire about it." Enlisted March 9th in New York City. Is his corps the 12th? Is 20th Corps right?

movements.letterExcerpt: I had, oh such a jolly good time this morning. What do you think? I received no less than six letters from home. It did seem so good to hear from you all again. The letters were from April 27th to May...
movements.notes: **SIX LETTERS FROM HOME — "oh such a jolly good time."** Letters from April 27 to May 18. Glad Mr. Bass convalescent — "he thinks flirting dangerous business." Dodds "a man of his age ought to know better." Bass had taste of bullets without going to war. **"OH, MOTHER, THAT IS MOST AS BAD AS THE BOY AND THE 'HUNDRED FOXES.'"** Mother's account — "a pailful of blood." "I have seen thousands of men wounded but hardly ever say anything come up to the pail of blood." Glad to have county bounty. Averill's charges — $190 making total $650, now taking out what he owes — nearly $100 — would leave all right. $500 in Mr. Savage's hands. "And does that leave my five hundred clear!" If paid shall send home $600. Fallen back toward Atlanta — resting 2 days. Start on after the Rebs in the morning. "May God be with us and grant us the victory." Culver Bostwick sends love — feels discouraged from writing. "Wished me to tell his friends that he is in the best of spirits." Send silk handkerchief.

movements.citation: Dyer's Compendium: 'Operations about Marietta and Kennesaw Mountain June 10-July 2'
movements.notes: Operations around Marietta. Pine Mountain, Lost Mountain, Kennesaw.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcome letter of May 21st a few days since. Am glad that you and Frances are both well. I accidentally saw in a newspaper a short time since that Buzzard's Roost is where Gen. Sherman...
movements.notes: Received welcome letter of May 21st. Frances and Mother both well. Saw in newspaper Buzzard's Roost — same as Gen. Sherman. Alex is not in Army of the Potomac — in Sherman's army. Glad of it. Letter from Alex dated B. Roost. **JOSEPH MARTIN $400 TO WIFE** — Frenchman from Champlain. $20 of his $400 sent by express — "twenty dollars of this money is sent by Joseph Martin to his wife." Newspapers very acceptable. **JAMES TALKING WITH SOLDIERS** — soldiers said $800 bounty; he rec'd $860. James also rec'd one month's pay making $873. Due: James yet $75 NY State bounty and $242 U.S. — to be paid at different times. Wishes Frances would keep account of money sent home. **FORAGING** — rode out with long wagon train 15 miles. Rode out and walked back. Wagon train came where corn houses were — "plenty pulled off the side boards of the barns and filled the wagons with corn." $828 had the husks on. The women did not like to see the corn taken.

movements.letterExcerpt: By the kind providence of God I am permitted to write you again, and inform you that I am still uninjured. We have been fighting nearly every day since I last wrote you and working the greater portion...
movements.notes: **FIGHTING NEARLY EVERY DAY.** "We have been fighting nearly every day since I last wrote you and working the greater portion of every night (and sometimes the whole) entrenching ourselves in positions gained the previous day." Camp in field near Marietta. **DRIVEN ENEMY FROM TWO STRONG LINES OF ENTRENCHMENTS** — "now burrowing away at him in his third." Yesterday Holy Sabbath — passed in quiet meditation. "But far different was it with the 60th N.Y. Vets." Were advance regt of division — **deployed as skirmishers, kept engaged with enemy from two P.M. until after ten o'clock last night** — when relieved. **KILLED AND WOUNDED LIST PILING UP FEARFULLY.** None of boys from Champlain injured. Relieved from front line this morning by 2nd — "not entirely out of range as the whistle of an occasional bullet plainly tells us." Batteries keeping up pretty steady fire — skirmish lines also pretty hotly engaged. Rebel sharpshooters "keeping up a pretty lively fire on one of our batteries on the hill just above us, but with not much effect." No word from James. Received letter May 21st; letter and papers from Mrs. Boyle. "Keep a stout heart. We are all in God's hands. May He grant us all submission to His will." N.Y. Tribune and papers — "how you all are I receive the papers oftener than the letters." Mail delayed at Chattanooga — difficulty of transportation. "How little the people at the North realize how much our country has cost us." Send silk handkerchief — by mail in form of package.

movements.letterExcerpt: We are still encamped on the Mississippi; how long we shall remain here I cannot tell. I heard this morning that it was probable that we should not remain here long. The location is a good one, and if...
movements.notes: **JAMES'S FIRST LETTER IN THE COLLECTION.** Still on Mississippi — probably won't remain long. Location is good — would not object to remaining. **FORAGING EXPEDITION** — one trial of marching, pretty hard day's work. "I stood it pretty well considering I had used my legs so little since I have entered the service." Small town — filled wagon train of 100 wagons from French woman's barn. French like their masters. **NEGROES** quite plenty in town — "all spoke French like their masters." In front of some houses were squads of 8-10 all sitting as radiantly as a negro. Handsome brick houses — pretty yards in front. Sugar in mills along river — "does not benefit us any." Foraging strictly forbidden. **JAMES SWEENEY** — lately come into regt. as surgeon. Was a little faller when he left our place — "I think that if either of us are sick he will be a friend worth having." "Comment vous portez ma vous?" What do you think of this war? "Do you watch the Army of the Potomac with interest?"
Transferred east with 153rd NY. Arrived Shenandoah Valley.

movements.letterExcerpt: As James wrote you yesterday I will write a few lines also and send with him today. We have been waiting to hear from you before we wrote, but as no letter comes will wait no longer.
movements.notes: Brief note — James wrote yesterday, Charles adds a few lines. Waiting to hear from home. **DR. JAMES SWEENEY** — new doctor wanted to see the two Hubbells. He told us he saw Frances about 3 weeks before. Sociable. Regt. has had only one surgeon since it left Washington till now. $400 sent by express — paid $4 freight and $2 insurance.
Assault on Kennesaw Mountain.

movements.letterExcerpt: If any additional charge is made please let me know the amount, so I can collect of Martin his share of the freight. He has paid his share of the $5.00 which was 30¢.
movements.notes: **FRAGMENT — beginning on previous PDF page.** Chaplain says will not stay here a great while — will garrison someplace near Mississippi. Butter plenty but sell high. Flour 10-12½¢/lb. Dried apples 25¢/lb. Dried apple pies 50¢ each. Small short cakes 5¢. Pies and flour cakes made by men — baked in kettle with cover. James making doughnuts — fried grease out of pork, no yeast powder, cakes heavy. Wanted sugar or molasses — 50¢ or over at sutlers. Drew flour once in a while. New York papers sell for 25¢. Haven't heard from Alex lately. Frances prosper?

movements.letterExcerpt: You see I am going to write you a long letter while I have the chance for we shall probably be "heels over head" in the din and turmoil of the fight in a day or two. The "Johnnies" don't like the way ...
movements.notes: **FRAGMENT — date uncertain, "July (?) —— (186 4)."** "Heels over head in the din and turmoil of the fight in a day or two." Johnnies don't like Sherman's fights — "they say he comes around on the blind side of them and they have to 'up and git.'" Old lady — Yanks made three lines of fight in her yard and tipped over barrel of ashes — "she would not have taken two dollars and a half or any sum of money for those 'ashes.'" "They had a man killed and went off and wouldn't kote him off with them." **60TH NY SKIRMISHING REGT OF BRIGADE.** First night — close to rebel lines, terrible stare. Talking, shouting, coughing all night. Called out "three cheers for Genl. Hardee" — "the setup a — mmh well, I cannot describe it." **GENL. BARKER THOUGHT KILLED** — was killed a short time since, great rejoicings. Alexander saw old fellow riding along as sound as a dollar the next day. "It was Genl. Barker that was killed." **20TH CORPS ("STAR MEN") — "HOOKER'S REGT."** "You can tell M. H. Cook that the Eastern troops are considerably above par in this department." 14th Corps (Genl. Logan) now holds that part of line. 13th N.Y. Battery brought out. Feeling of animosity between eastern and western troops is dying away. Speech of Genl. McClellan pleased him — "the right kind of ring to it... the way he spoke of the officers of the regular army who had proved traitors to their country."
Embarked from Louisiana by ship. Emergency transfer east to counter Early's Raid.

movements.letterExcerpt: Must try and write you a word at least though I am pretty tired as I was up all night working with pick and shovel in the trenches. Our batteries along the whole line opened up on the rebs this mornin...
movements.notes: In the field near Marietta, Ga. Pretty tired — up all night working with pick and shovel in trenches. Batteries along whole line opened up on rebs — sharp skirmishing and shot from batteries. Settled down again to usual opening — "i.e. — sharp skirmishing and a shot now and then from the batteries." Movements being made — "will bring matters to a decided issue soon." **LUTHER WOUNDED.** "I had just gone up with several men to an old house from which we intended to get the log. When the Capt. (I was at work with the shovels) ordered me with several others to go on and give them a lift in bringing it down." Ball whistled close — "a yell of agony." Luther — "he thought he was not much hurt — that he thought that it was only a flesh wound." Ball tore a furrow in right side — passed through fleshy part of right arm a little above elbow. **NOT DANGEROUS** — laid up two or three months. "God in his kindness great kindness has as yet preserved me from all harm." Culver Bostwick also well. "Culver and I are getting worn down bully thin. We suffer terribly from the heat — and — and terrain — if I must say it."
Crossing of the Chattahoochee River.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of June 20th yesterday and the handkerchief enclosed, for which I am very, very much obliged. I can now wipe the perspiration from my brow with some degree of comfort — before I...
movements.notes: In field near Chattahoochee, Ga. Received letter of June 20th and handkerchief — "can now wipe the perspiration from my brow with some degree of comfort." Before receiving handkerchief was "reduced to the necessity of using a portion of an old rebel meal bag." Fighting will all be done this summer. **"EYES OF THE 60TH VETS HAVE BEEN BLEST WITH A SIGHT OF THE GOAL"** — yesterday were on a high ridge and could see the city (Atlanta) with its tall spires and chimneys, great smoke going up from its numerous furnaces. With glass could see windows, houses, streets plainly. Forts around city, lines of rifle pits. "We are not fighting much at present, only skirmishing and an occasional shot from the batteries." Last night about dusk "there was a furious cannonade." Skirmishers very sharp — "we were too distant to tell." About midnight firing of skirmishers very sharp — "expected we should be called up but it settled down." Rebel works on a ridge close to its banks — "they are very strong, I should judge." They have several large earthen forts. **BISHOP POLK KILLED** — "the cannon fired that killed Bishop Polk as our Regt. was close to the batteries at the time. The shot or shell struck him in the breast. If the shell had burst, old Johnston and Hardee would probably ave shared the same fate, as they were close beside him." Presidential campaign — "is there much excitement up there relative to the Presidential campaign?" Fremont will meet little favor with army. Democratic convention at Chicago — "they have shown the right spirit and put the Republicans to shame." Every nerve should be used to strengthen armies and uphold administration. "It will be time enough to talk politics after the summer's work is done."

movements.letterExcerpt: How different this Sabbath morning is with you to what it is with us. Instead of the chime of the church bells our ears are saluted with the roar of cannon and bursting shell. (I commenced since one b...
movements.notes: Near Atlanta, Ga. Sabbath morning — "how different this Sabbath morning is with you to what it is with us. Instead of the chime of the church bells our ears are saluted with the roar of cannon and bursting shell." (Another shell made us jump a little just now.) **MOST TERRIFIC BATTLE THE 20TH INST.** — "the rebs were defeated with great loss, leaving their dead and a large number of wounded upon the field." None of boys from Champlain hurt. **CAPT. DELANEY WOUNDED** — in the arm, pretty bad but not dangerous. Will be away 2-3 months. "The 60th Vets covered themselves with glory." Credit for saving 13th N.Y. Independent Battery. **REBS SHOOTING UNCOMFORTABLY CLOSE** — "I must hurry up and say what I have to say as it is a little dangerous writing out here." **WITHIN 1¼ MILES OF ATLANTA** — long range guns shelling the city. "How good God has been to me."

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of the 11th inst. and paper of the 12th last evening and was much pleased with its contents. They were the right thing in the right place. I am writing this letter upon the pape...
movements.notes: Near Atlanta, Ga. Received letter of 11th inst. and paper of 12th. "It is singular that I receive the papers so much sooner than the letters." Writing on paper you sent. Rebel batteries opened so furiously — obliged to seek safety in works. One man had arm blown off, two battery horses killed. **BATTERIES SILENT BY SHERMAN'S ORDER** — about 10 P.M. opened lustily. **"ATLANTA EXPRESS"** — shell into city every five minutes during night. **POSITION CHANGED — further to left.** 15th, 16th, 17th corps moved to right — heavy cannonading, heavy fight. **REGT. SENT FOR FEINT ATTACK** — "right smart" of shooting. Rebs opened heavy fire from batteries. Lost two men. Health very good. James and Charles have not written — received only one letter from Charles since in the Department. Capt. Ransom letter received. Handkerchief received. Frances gone to Charlotte.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter of July 17th and 18th a day or two since and was pleased to hear that you are all well and considerably surprised to hear the 153d was in Maryland. I knew that Gen'l. Canby's tr...
movements.notes: Near Atlanta, Ga. Received letters of July 17th and 18th. Surprised to hear 153rd was in Maryland — knew Gen'l. Canby's troops there, didn't suppose 153rd among them. **HEAVY CANNONADE — extreme left.** 23rd Corps (Gen'l. Schofield) moving to right. Object: **STRIKE MACON AND ATLANTA RAILROAD.** Lines within half mile of road. Sunday night constructing new line of work — obliged to work at night on account of rebel sharpshooters. **SHARPSHOOTER HIT THE MAIL** — ball "spot" into center of crowd collecting mail; passed through tent. "It made them jump a little but they did not scatter until they had got their letters." James and Charles haven't written — "Why does not James write!" Feels neglected. "I would do almost anything for him."
Sheridan's Valley Campaign begins Aug 7. Operations toward Winchester.

movements.letterExcerpt: [At the top of the letter was written: "My dearest child; Write me immediately."]
movements.notes: Near Atlanta, Ga. At top of letter: **"My dearest child; Write me immediately."** Received letter July 25th, papers ("Times" and "Tribune"), envelopes, paper. "Now, 'ain't' I a good boy?" McPherson and Schofield moved to right — battle — forces victorious, driving enemy 1½ miles, taking fort and battery, **CUTTING ONLY REMAINING ROAD.** **HOOKER HAS LEFT US** — "He had endeared himself to the whole corps. The day he left he rode along the line bidding the men goodbye." Man from Pennsylvania regt. had leg taken off by cannon shot — being carried off on stretcher — **"Good bye, General Hooker!"** — "It seemed to have moved the Gen'l. greatly. He got off his horse, took off his hat and went up and shook hands with the poor fellow, making some kind encouraging words at the same time." **"THE 20TH CORPS WILL NEVER FORGET OLD 'FIGHTING JOE.'"** Maj. Gen'l. Slocum now commands. Charles and James on Peninsula with Grant. Report of Charles being ill — hopes not true. "I hope James will try and bear his disappointment like a man. I am afraid it is he instead of Charles that is ill." Frances at C. Not received tea yet. Culver Bostwick received some. Regards to Mrs. Brikerhoff.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your kind letter of July 10th some days since, but knowing as you do how we soldiers are situated on an active campaign, I trust you will excuse my tardiness in answering. My Mother was rig...
movements.notes: Near Atlanta, Ga. Received Ransom's letter of July 10th. "I have so much to write that I hardly know where to begin." Theatre of most active operations: extreme right. Combined attack of **HOWARD (FORMERLY McPHERSON'S) AND SCHOFIELD** very successful — **LAST REMAINING RAILROAD SEVERED.** "I hope we shall be able to bag the Johnnies here, for I am heartily tired of chasing them." Heavy siege train being brought up. **HARDEST FIGHTING SINCE CROSSING CHATTAHOOCHEE.** "A long list of casualties that would frighten a man just to look at it." **BATTLE OF PEACHTREE CREEK** — "The fight of the 20th of July was an awful one. The rebels threw their men upon us in solid columns and seemed bound to drive us into the Chattahoochee. But we were not to be driven." Changed front three times during battle — "matters looked a little 'scaly' when I saw the rebs coming up in our rear." **60TH AND 147TH PENN. SAVED TWO DIVISION BATTERIES.** Rebs had use of Bundy's battery guns. 60th only regiment not broken during fight. At Lost Mountain — 60th only regt. to reach top. Capt. Delaney wounded fight of 20th. **P. H. BROOKWAY COMMISSIONED** — in command of Co. H. Elliott now Major; Thomas Lieut./Col.; Goddard Colonel. **CONSOLIDATION** with 134th N.Y. coming. Surplus officers and NCOs to be reduced.

movements.letterExcerpt: It is a long while since I have written you. I think my last letter was from Morganza. Since that time our regt. has seen considerable hardship. We left Louisiana the last of June for the North — this...
movements.notes: Baltimore, Md. (Frederick City hospital). Long while since written — last letter from Morganza. Left Louisiana last of June for North. **EARLY'S RAID — WASHINGTON DEFENSES.** Placed in rifle pits; heavy skirmishing; rebs retreated. Sent as reserve for 6th Corps — followed rebs to Shenandoah Valley. 6th Corps skirmishing but Johnnies did not want to fight. Crossed river, lay in belt of woods expecting fight — enemy only wanted to get off with plunder. Ordered to report Washington within 24 hours. **NIGHT MARCH — EXHAUSTION.** Four men came in with dressed porker. Pig hitting briskly that afternoon. **HARDTACK DESCRIBED** — "Bake a flour and water cake with no salt or saleratus on a griddle till it is hard." Waded river, marched until four next day. **FELL OUT** — blistered foot, fatigue, want of sleep. Wagon train. Chainbridge. Shoes and clothes issued. Marched to Harper's Ferry, then counter march. **FREDERICK CITY HOSPITAL** — two weeks. "My sickness was generally unwell and played out." Hospital on hill overlooking city. Milk 16¢/qt, peaches 80¢/bu. **INDIGNATION ABOUT EARLY'S RAID** — 20,000 troops around Washington (veterans), rebel force only 15,000. Army came up, harvested, plundered, got off with wagon train three miles long. **CHARLIE'S HEALTH** — thin and used up, finds marches hard. "Charlie is one of the kind that'll go until he cannot go." Soft bread, pilot bread, meat twice a day, stewed apples.

movements.letterExcerpt: You perceive that I am again in the hospital. I am not wounded but am afflicted with what the surgeon calls genuine scurvy. He says I am very young to have it. By taking good care of myself and with p...
movements.notes: 2d Div. Hospital, 20th Corps, near Atlanta. **SCURVY** — "afflicted with what the surgeon calls genuine scurvy. He says I am very young to have it." Needs vegetables. Received letter Aug 8th — Dixon brought it. Wants Tribune with acct. of battle of 20th. Heavy artillery and musketry heard — battle on right, rebs charging works, repulsed with terrible slaughter. "Their loss, it is said, is to be counted by the thousand." Rebs under influence of liquor. Reports conflicting — "hardly dare write them." Lieut. Brookway has charge of mail. Using last stamps. Mrs. Frances returned? Received her letter — "didn't see my boots for a week after." James and Charles — fears groundless about being prisoners. **F. A. COOK HOT FOR LINCOLN.** "I will hoist my colors soon." **WILL VOTE** — over 21 by muster rolls. "You know I will have been in the service over three years when the election comes off."

movements.letterExcerpt: I received a letter from you last night dated Aug. 20th, was glad to hear from you, but am very sorry you are so anxious about James and me. James, I think, is all right. When around for a couple of d...
movements.notes: Camp near Harper's Ferry. James sent to hospital at Frederick — Dr. Sweeney told Charles he would send James as soon as he could. James thin in flesh, had diarrhea. "But I think James is having a good time in some hospital or convalescent camp." James doesn't care about letter writing. Charles in **CONVALESCENT DEPT** — nearly two weeks. More clerks than necessary — may go back to regt. "I have flatted in considerably since I have been here because I eat all the sugar I want." Sending recipes for diarrhea. Man with chronic diarrhea — "a perfect skeleton." **$5 WASTED TELEGRAPHING ABOUT JAMES.** Entirely out of money and postage stamps. Army composed of 19th and 6th Corps, also 8th — all under **GEN. SHERIDAN** who has large force of cavalry. Haven't had sight of rebs yet — cavalry fought with them.

movements.letterExcerpt: Now that I am in a hospital I know you will be anxious to hear from me often and consequently I shall endeavor to be very regular in my correspondence. I am getting along as well as can be expected, t...
movements.notes: 2d Div. Hospital, 20th A.C. Now in hospital — will endeavor to be very regular in correspondence. Getting along as well as can be expected — scurvy will take some time. "I have very good care taken of me." Received letter Aug 16th — very sorry to hear James is sick in hospital and Charley likely to be soon. "I had a hearty laugh when I took in the idea of your three hopeful sons being in the hospital at the one and same time." Agrees not something to laugh at — "low diet and doctor's medicines are not quite as agreeable as some things." **CORPS FALLEN BACK FROM ATLANTA** — holding line along Chattahoochee. Rest of army gone on grand flanking excursion, heading toward Macon. **REPORTED REBS HAVE LEFT ATLANTA AND GONE AFTER SHERMAN.** Stirring things will happen. **SLOCUM NOW COMMANDS 6TH CORPS** [sic — should be 20th]. 1st Lieut. P. H. Brookway (formerly Orderly Sergt. of Co. H.) now commands Co. Capt. Delaney at home. Chronic diarrhea will not get hold of James and Charles. "It is a terrible disease."

movements.letterExcerpt: The evening of the day I wrote you my last letter, I with a large number of other sick and wounded was put on board a hospital train and sent to this place. We were two nights and a day getting here. ...
movements.notes: U.S. General Hospital, Chattanooga, Tenn. Sent from front with large number of sick and wounded on hospital train. **WHEELER'S RAID** — "We should have gone directly to Nashville, but old Wheeler had made a raid and torn up the road so we were obliged to stop here." Pretty sick yesterday and last night — much better today. Should be able to join regt. before a great while. **CHICAGO CONVENTION** — considerable anxiety about Presidential nominee. "We will know in a day or two." Nothing of interest to write.

movements.letterExcerpt: Much to my gratification a day or two since the 60th N.Y. Vets. were sent to this place from the front to escort the Paymaster of the 20th Corps down, and of course they brought what mail there was fo...
movements.notes: U.S. Field Hospital No. 2, Chattanooga, Tenn. Much to gratification — **60TH NY VETS SENT TO ESCORT PAYMASTER OF 20TH CORPS.** Brought mail — "I had not heard from you in a long, long, time." Too much uncertainty to have mail sent here. Getting along pretty well but may take long time to get scurvy out of blood. "However I guess I will be all right before long." **MAN GAVE OLD DRINK OF LIME WATER** — something similar to lemonade. "Then I say lime I don't mean lime such as they make mortar of, but limes, a fruit like lemons." **LUTHER WITH REGT** — has been up to see Alexander twice. Pleasant to have them here. Regt still here unless they have left this morning. "I am sorry I shall not be able to draw pay with the regt. this time." **GOVERNMENT OWES $240.** Can draw a little here — sufficient for wants but no more. **"NO WAY TO PUT DOWN THIS REBELLION BUT BY FORCE OF ARMS."** "A few more vigorous pushes will shove them into the Atlantic Ocean." When you speak of tomatoes, potatoes, etc. — "I long to be there to enjoy these good things." Received money and everything — "perhaps you did not put on enough postage for the tea." Tell Fannie — will try and write her before a great while. "If any body wants to know my political principles you tell them I am a 'war man.'"

movements.notes: U.S. Hospital No. 2, Chattanooga, Tenn. **THREE YEARS IN SERVICE.** "Have you taken a realizing sense that I have now been in the U.S. Service as a soldier three years — three long — long — weary years!" "Three years ago today I took an oath to serve the United States of America faithfully as a soldier for the term of 'three years or the war.'" "I have with God's help done my best to bear that oath and do my duty as a soldier should do." **"And now, dear Mother, I want you to join me, (and I know you will) in thanking God for his kind and watchful care over me."** Heart too full to speak. First time in general hospital sick — "You know I was in one last fall but then I was wounded." Getting along very well — **BLIND AS A BAT AT NIGHT.** "There are a number here troubled in the same way." **HEAVY FIGHT IN SHENANDOAH VALLEY** — morning papers. Very anxious to hear from boys.

movements.letterExcerpt: I shall now only write an apology for a letter and shall conclude with a promise of a long letter before a great while, and I hope I shall find grace in your eyes. I do not feel very well today, and I...
movements.notes: U.S. Field Hospital No. 2, Chattanooga, Tenn. Brief apology for not writing — "I shall now only write an apology for a letter and shall conclude with a promise of a long letter before a great while." Does not feel very well today — "I trust you will regard this as a sufficient excuse for these few lines." "I only write them to let you know I have not forgotten you."

movements.letterExcerpt: I sit down to write you a few lines, feeling very thankful that James came out of the battle near Winchester two days since unhurt. There were four killed and twelve wounded in our Co. James is lookin...
movements.notes: In the field near Strasburg. **BATTLE NEAR WINCHESTER** — two days since, came out unhurt. **4 KILLED, 12 WOUNDED in Co.** James looking very well — nicely recruited. Day or two after Dr. Sweeney wrote, James rejoined regt. Still with Brigade Commissary — "getting fat, the result of good living." Have to walk on march but carry no load. Received letter with $2 and stamps. Also James rec'd 3 newspapers. **JAMES GOT CAPT. TO WRITE ALBANY** for state bounty — $25 — should have had it long since. Mother's investment in "2d hands" may well pay. **CAMPED NEAR BERRYVILLE** two weeks — reason James has not written. Lost good many men in fight two days since — whipped rebs, drove them to this place. **REGT. LOST 55 WOUNDED AND 10 KILLED.** Near Winchester — about 12 miles this side. (Written on back — note from Frances.)

movements.letterExcerpt: Now for the long promised letter. You perceive I am still in the same place, but I am unable to say how long I may remain here. I am getting along very well, I think, and will doubtless be able to joi...
movements.notes: U.S. Field Hospital No. 2, Chattanooga, Tenn. Long political letter. Still in hospital — continues to be blind at night. **SOLDIERS WILL VOTE FOR McCLELLAN.** "A majority of the border state men, I thin, will, and a large number of the 'Hibernians.'" They don't like the "nigger" nor any man that favors them. **"NIGGER EQUALITY"** — border men get quite wrathy. "They say they would rejoice to see the niggers free if they would be sent out of the country, lest to have the nection among them on an equality with the white man they never would agree to it." **ALEXANDER SYMPATHIZES WITH BORDER MEN** — "I could never consent to see these black men mingled with our white and form a part of the people of the United States." "I do not think it was ever the design of Providence that the two races should be mingled." "It will do to talk about this 'equality' matter when the war is over." **VOTING AGE** — now over 21 by U.S. service laws. Sept 27 — weather chilly, rain. Would like ripe apples, steamed apple dumplings. Last letter received from home dated August — very anxious. May be with regt. soon.

movements.letterExcerpt: As the mail leaves soon I will write a few lines. I rejoined the regt. the last day of Sept. There were too many clerks there in the commissary so they told two of us to go to our regts. I am quite fa...
movements.notes: Harrisonburg, Shenandoah Valley. **REJOINED REGT. last day of Sept.** Too many clerks in commissary — told to go back. Quite fat and in good health. James very well. No gun yet — turned in gun when left regt. **RECRUIT FROM FRESSEVILLE — $1,202 BOUNTY.** Enlisted one year. About 90 miles from Harper's Ferry. **CAVALRY BURNED BARNS AND GRIST MILLS** as far as Stanton (Staunton). Advanced 8 miles for flour, came back. Troops suffered from want of rations — wagoned from Harper's Ferry. On march, foraged: "pigs, sheep, chickens, apples, butter, etc." Provost Marshall can't stop it. Rich valley — fine farming country. Many wounded rebs in hospital. Recruits coming fast. **BURNED ALL FENCES** — oak rails make good fire. Water and wood scarce. Soldiers daily duty: "cook, clean his gun and look over his clothes and pick off the vermin." **"A man is no soldier unless he is lousy."** Some think going to Louisiana. $75 from Albany — James's state bounty?

movements.letterExcerpt: When did I write you last! I know it is a long time since. Do not think because I have not written you that I have forgotten you. We have had two fights of which you have undoubtedly heard, driving th...
movements.notes: Harrisonburg, Shenandoah Valley. Started Oct 4, continued Oct 12. **TWO FIGHTS — driving rebels both times.** Last pursuit — inhabitants said rebs went through "with a rush," army demoralized. Passed several burning wagons in night pursuit. "You have travelled this road once, I think." **OCT 12 — FALLEN BACK TO CEDAR CREEK NEAR STRASBURG.** Burning barns and forage as they went. **ALEX DOUGLAS MISSING — GUERRILLAS.** Fell to rear with one man — not seen or heard of since. Boys running through houses taking what they choose — "exasperates the rebels very much." "This other fellow from our company was one of the greatest house thieves in our regt." "Ma, there is a Yankee down cellar taking all our preserves and bacon." "Ma, see that Yankee looking in the oven." Little boy of brigade gobbled while foraging — shot up with rebel deserters — slipped out during fight. **LETTER FROM HOME** — Mother says Alex quite ill. "I have seen one month in the hospital since I enlisted." Charley's health now pretty good. Some talk about going to Louisiana. **ELECTION** — "I'm a voter; I go for old Abe; he is the man." Little Mac will probably run strong. War lasted nearly four years — "I would like to see it ended."
Returned to duty briefly. Shenandoah Valley operations.

movements.letterExcerpt: You perceive I have again changed my quarters. I was sent from Chattanooga last Wednesday and reached here Friday morning. The hospital I am now in is a very good one and I am getting along famously. ...
movements.notes: U.S.A. Hospital No. 3, Nashville, Tenn. Sent from Chattanooga last Wednesday. Hospital is very good. Asked doctor to let him go to regiment — said he would see about it. Eyes much better. **LINCOLN SEEMS FAVORED.** "When we were coming from Chattanooga a vote was taken in the car I was in. Thirty-seven voted for Lincoln and five for McClellan." Tried for furlough at Chattanooga — doctor "did not do right." Gave furlough to fellow with scurvy "not near so bad as I did, and when I asked him he said 'he would like to but, but, but, etc.'" War will be over before long — shall need no furlough. Anxious to get back to regt. for letters. **FLAG RAISED AT FORT GILLAM today.** James and Charles have written.

movements.notes: Camp near Strasburg, Va. **BATTLE OF CEDAR CREEK (Oct 19, 1864).** "James and I rec'd a lot of newspapers Oct. 18th and were anticipating a good deal of pleasure next day in reading them. Well, next morning I was awakened by a sharp volley of musketry. James exclaimed, 'The Rebs are here!'" **SURPRISE ATTACK** — jumped up, accoutrements, fell in behind breastworks, ordered to pack up, tents down in a jiffy. "By that time the rebs were close to us. It was a surprise attack. They got behind our breastworks before we knew it." Brigade ordered to leave breastworks, form on other side of deep ravine. Jumped breastworks — "the Rebs were firing into us and we were moving up the hill the bullets came very thick." **JAMES WOUNDED** — flesh wound in thigh or hip, walked about five miles to hospital. "Says James had made a bandage of his drawers." **JAMES LUCAS REPORTED KILLED** — shot through head and arm. **SGT. PELKIER (PELKY) FROM CORBEAU** shot through leg. **ALEX DOUGLAS MISSING** about ten or twelve days — captured or killed with another man. Guerrillas. "Every one is very sorry about Douglas as he was very much liked." **LIEUT. COL. STRAIN WOUNDED** in arm in fight of 19th Oct. **REGT. HAD ABOUT 50 WOUNDED AND 8 KILLED. CO. HAD 7 WOUNDED AND 2 KILLED.** "The Rebs drove us out of our camp in the morning when we lost a great many men, but we rallied and drove them, recapturing all our artillery and all of theirs. We drove them out of our camp and beyond to Fisher's Hill." Rebs came in by flank where 8th Corps lay. Very thankful not scratched. Very sorry about Lucas. Dr. Sweeney letter?

movements.letterExcerpt: You can have no idea how anxious I am to hear from you all and I have at length determined to have a letter directed here. So please, immediately on receipt of this, write me a long letter telling me ...
movements.notes: U.S.A. Hospital No. 3, Nashville, Tenn. "You can have no idea how anxious I am to hear from you all." Wants letter directed here. **WOULD NOT TAKE OATH** prescribed in NY voting law — "have consequently lost my chance of voting." **"COULD I HAVE VOTED I SHOULD HAVE CAST IT 'SQUARE AND FAIR' FOR ABRAHAM LINCOLN."** "The majority of soldiers will vote that way." Ten (perhaps more) days longer.

movements.letterExcerpt: I had a letter written and sealed which I carried in my pocket for a long time. I have now determined to add another before I send it to you. I was wounded in the left thigh at Cedar Run. It is nothin...
movements.notes: Patterson Park Hospital, Baltimore, Md. **WOUNDED AT CEDAR CREEK** — "I was wounded in the left thigh at Cedar Run. It is nothing but a flesh wound and is doing well." Walked several miles after being hit to avoid capture. Forces driving Johnnies full well — "things changed before night." **ARMY COMPLETELY DEMORALIZED** — "They threw away everything. We got their wagon train, artillery and almost everything they had." Johnnies attacked, routed 8th Corps before daylight. "This rather took our force by surprise and compelled them to retreat as they were flanked and the breastworks would be of no use." **"I DO NOT BELIEVE THE REBS WILL TRY IT AGAIN IN THE VALLEY — three times terribly whipped."** Company very much cut up — "scarcely anything left of it." Lucas badly wounded. **HOSPITAL IN BALTIMORE** — rode in army wagon, then freight car. Thirty miles to railroad station, then 100+ in freight car. Baltimore comfortable. **LINCOLN WILL BE ELECTED.** "I shall be able to vote here and shall cast my vote for Abraham Lincoln." Not been paid for six months.

movements.letterExcerpt: I read your letter announcing grandmothers death two days since. Was not surprised as she was so old. I suppose Aunt Mary will come North if she can get away.
movements.notes: Camp at Cedar Creek, Va. **GRANDMOTHER'S DEATH** announced — letter received. Not surprised — "she was so old." Aunt Mary will come North. Have not heard from James since last fight — wound not dangerous. Chaplain says James walked to hospital. James Lucas shot through head and arm — "I did not see him." Sgt. Pelkier (Pelky) shot through leg. Alex Douglas missing — guerrillas. **CO. NOW NUMBERS ONLY 22.** "In two fights we lost twenty-three men killed and wounded." Lost two in this valley. "In the fight bullets flew all around me but I came out without a scratch." **VOTED FOR LINCOLN.** **"ONLY TWO VOTES FOR LINCOLN IN OUR CO."** De Sweeney was taken prisoner morning of fight — came back that night. "Did not know what had become of James until that night after dark." Sunday 6th — called up at 4 o'clock, stood to arms all day, stood to arms till daylight.
At Nashville. 60th NY consolidated. Preparing for Battle of Nashville.

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your welcome letter of Nov. 22nd today containing one dollar & a silk Hdkf. also fine comb. Am sorry that the people of Champlain are in such trouble about the rebs in Canada. Think that th...
movements.notes: Camp near Newtown, Va. Received letter with dollar and silk handkerchief — "also fine comb." Trouble about rebs in Canada — "Think that the alarm is needless." Seven months pay due — daily expecting to be paid. Dollar will be all he needs. "Do you know how much the Hdkf. Alex sent me cost. It is almost too nice for a soldier." Not surprised to hear of Alex being home — he is not of age (soldier age) and therefore not entitled to vote — "But am glad that he got the furlough. He was very lucky. I wish he could get into the Invalid Corps." Best place for him. James doing well. Not heard from him directly, but a Sergt. who went with James to hospital, recd from him some time since. **ELECTION DAY — Nov 8th.** Called up very early, cooked breakfast, stood to arms all day — didn't move. Next morning called up, marched after a few hours. "Did not march till ten oclock, when we reached here after a few hours march." Good winter quarters — "quite large & have a stone fireplace & chimney." "Have been very busy which is the reason that I have not wrote." **DEC 9TH — SIX MONTHS PAY LAST NIGHT — $108.** Signed the pay rolls some days since. **DEC 10TH** — six inches of snow. Regt. going to guard railroad 10 miles from here. **THANKSGIVING** — turkey dinner, but ration for three was so small "we annexed it to off for four big hard tacks." Hard tack better. "I have bought it at the commissary." Plenty to do — roll calls, reviews, guard duty, backing wood from woods, etc. Brigade review next Sunday. **Frances wants to know how he looks** — "I wear mustache & chin whiskers, look quite savage, shave the side of my face every week or two — could oftener but no razor." Lost two teeth in valley. "I do not think I have straightened any since I left home, but am as round shouldered as ever." Letter from Frances and two Tribunes received. **BOOTS, TOWEL, COLORED HANDKERCHIEF** requested. Enclosed $50.

movements.letterExcerpt: You perceive I am again in Nashville. We left Chattanooga the same day I wrote you my last letter and were two days in getting to this place. We were obliged to move very cautiously as the telegraph w...
movements.notes: Nashville, Tenn. Back in Nashville from Chattanooga — left same day as last letter. **BUILDING BREASTWORKS** — been hard at work for last few days. "Hood is now in front of the city." Skirmishing and artillery firing tolerably brisk. Troops still hard at work strengthening fortifications. **"HOOD OF THE BOGUS CONFEDERACY WILL HAVE TO WHISTLE FOR HIS SUPPER"** — "so far as getting it out of the storehouse of Nashville is concerned." Hope to get to regiment soon — "I do not like my place here." **Officers drink altogether too much whiskey.** **FORT NEGLEY** — close by, now using heavy guns upon the rebs. "Please write as often and direct to A. F. Hubbell, Nashville, Tenn. Do not put on economy and rest."

movements.letterExcerpt: I received your letter, papers and package this morning. All were directed Walnut Hill, but they got here nevertheless. The vest is a very nice one, fits very well, and is very comfortable. You took t...
movements.notes: Chestnut Hill Hospital, Philadelphia. Received letter, papers, package. Directed to Walnut Hill but got here. **COAT DAMAGED — $16** put in Mr. Rich's hands. Keeler called. "We have had such a time in school this week which has resulted in the expelling of two girls — Miss Riley and Pocahontas — it was quite disgraceful." Mr. Webb, Mr. Averill — presented with democratic paper — "said he hoped that I would read it candidly." Mrs. Roe. "Her is grandmother; James Ransom is to take Mrs. Nebb's place." **THANKSGIVING** — "turkey and gravy, oyster soup (I could not eat that) boiled potatoes, bread, cranberry preserves and ice cream. All was cold." Each man had dinner piled on plate — ward got dinner about four o'clock, among last. **CAMPAIGN — DID NOT CARRY KNAPSACK** — carried bundle in sort of roll over right shoulder and under left arm. Far easier. **WOUND NEARLY HEALED.** Feel like getting back to regiment. **WRITING PAPER IN SMALL BOOK** for next campaign. Three tons of mail sent by sea to Savannah for Sherman's army. **RING ENCLOSED** — made several while on way last spring, broke in pocket book. Furloughs — so many out. **DID LT. COL. STRAIN LOSE A LEG?** Some say he did, others say not.

movements.letterExcerpt: Nothing of special interest has transpired here since I last wrote. Since then the weather has been intensely cold. Today the weather is clear, but very keen with about two inches of snow on the groun...
movements.notes: Nashville, Tenn. Nothing of special interest — intensely cold. "Just before the cold weather set in I'd set up in a shanty and fire place and am therefore quite comfortable." Out this morning beyond the pickets after rails for fire wood — "but was not fired at." **ADVANCE PICKETS — COLORED SOLDIER.** Got into pit of advance pickets (colored soldier) and reconnoitered the ground pretty thoroughly before going out. **"The colored gentleman told me he if he could 'only les get his eye onto one of dem rebs he would fetch him sure'"** — "and I rather think he would." **"THESE COLORED SOLDIERS FIGHT WELL."** Very little firing for last few days. Both sides keeping warm. "I hardly think the Johnny Rebs will venture to attack us in our present position." Expects **THOMAS WILL SOON TAKE THE OFFENSIVE.** Sherman will be at coast in a day or two. "I am heartily sick of my present position." **"RAIDERS" IN NORTHERN NEW YORK** — Nashville papers making fun of recent fright in Burlington, Vt. Militia and Home Guard still kept up.

movements.letterExcerpt: I wrote you a letter two days since requesting you to send me a pair of boots. Write now to say that I do not want the boots as I bought a pair of government boots last night. My letter of the 10th co...
movements.notes: Camp near Newtown, Va. Wrote requesting boots — now writes to say does not want them. Bought government boots last night — $1, letter of 10th containing fifty dollars. **WANTS MITTENS** — "one finger" style best, but given scarcity, hardly worth sending. Good pair of boots — paid only five dollars. Sutlers selling boots $10-15. **CAVALRY BOOTS.** About six inches of snow — very cold. Hard west wind, snow drifting. Weather is cause of being here. Expect to move soon — down to railroad and guarding. Must close — mail leaves soon.
Battle of Nashville. Decisive Union victory over Hood.
Post-battle. Pursuit of Hood then return to Nashville area.

movements.letterExcerpt: I recd. your letter of Dec. 20th two or three days since. Am very, very sorry that you have been so anxious about me, but bad news travels fast, as you heard no bad news it would have been better to h...
movements.notes: Camp Russell, near Newtown, Va. Recd letter of Dec 20th. "Am very, very sorry that you have been so anxious about me, but bad news travels fast." Enclosed $20. After taxes, if money left, can invest in three year 7-30 Bonds. **WROTE JAMES** yesterday advising not to hurry about coming back. Recd letter from James — says he will be back soon. **CHRISTMAS** — "all the men had a ration of whiskey which is now a gill." Enclosed $20. Frances going to school through snow drifts. **HAVE NOT WRITTEN ALEX YET** — will wait till he rejoins regt. If he was with regt., would have had chance to help take Savannah — lucky that he missed march of 500 miles. Hore war nearly over — "but have not much faith that it is." If it lasts, James and Alex will be in it. **LAST NIGHT BRIGADE GAVE ROUSING CHEERS** when told of fall of Savannah. **DR. SWEENEY** called at tent — showed letter he had read from Alexander. Told Charles he had written Alexander two or three days before. When? On march last fall "De Sweeney did all he could for James & I." Has been a friend. **LT. COL. STRAIN** — one who got Alexander place at commissary at Banks HQ. Very friendly. Must stop — going on picket. "Please send me some postage stamps as I am entirely out. Think James has no stamps."
Continued winter camp. Garrison duty in the Valley.

movements.letterExcerpt: I write in haste so that this letter will go by the steamer that leaves tonight. Our Regt. left Washington June 5th & landed here this morning. We lay all day yesterday at the mouth of the river waiti...
movements.notes: Savannah, Ga. Writing in haste — steamer leaves tonight. **Regt. left Washington June 5th.** Landed Savannah this morning. Lay at mouth of river — **man caught by tide while swimming, nearly carried to sea** — life preserver thrown, rescued by marines. City looks deserted — not much business. "My three years is on the 17th of Oct." Don't know if mustered out before. Joseph Martin $20 — requested.

movements.letterExcerpt: You have doubtless wondered at my long silence. I have been waiting to see if there would not soon be some news of our going home, but I still see no immediate prospects though I presume we will be di...
movements.notes: Near Washington, D.C. Long silence — waiting for news of going home. No immediate prospects — "I will still see no immediate prospects though I presume we will be discharged before a very very long while." Corps and division broken up. **GEN. GEARY** issued farewell order and gone. Veteran regts. formed into division commanded by **BREVET MAJ. GEN. GREENE** — "He was formerly Colonel of our Regt." Promoted to Brigadier. Commanded brigade in White Star Division. **WOUNDED AT WAUHATCHIE.** His son **CHRIS GREENE** (aide de camp) — "wounded a few weeks after his father at the battle of Ringgold. His leg was taken off by a cannon shot. Two of our Regt. bandaged his leg (it hung by a few muscles and these they were obliged to sever with a pocket knife) and carried him from the field. He presented each of them afterward with a handsome Star with his and their names engraved on them." Now on staff of his father. **$350 SENT HOME** — fifty dollar coupon bonds. Paymaster said money not well invested. Bought new watch — "I was obliged to sell my other watch to buy bread to keep life in me."

movements.letterExcerpt: I advised in my last letter home that my next should be to you, so here goes. My last letter was dated — I believe — the 16th of June. That's a naughty boy I have been I know you'll say, but I have be...
movements.notes: Near Alexandria, Va. **"THE LONG WISHED FOR ORDER CAME TO MUSTER THE SIXTIETH NEW YORK VETERAN VOLUNTEERS OUT OF THE UNITED STATES SERVICE IMMEDIATELY."** "That's a happy day that will be, eh, Miss Fannie, agreed and a proud one for me. God spare my life to see the time." **VALEDICTORY** — "When I left home nearly four years since our country was racked from its base to its center by one of the most violent and gigantic rebellions recorded on the pages of history. We knew not friends from foes. Treason walked our legislative halls and had command of our armies. Now by the providence of God, after four years of unparalleled struggling we stand a free and united nation, than which in point of honor we have no superior and in point of freedom, no equal." Letter from Mrs. Bostwick — Culver discharged a few days since.
Camp near Alexandria. Final processing.

movements.letterExcerpt: The last letter we received from you said, that at Uncle Henry's request you were going to Charlotte. Perhaps that is the reason we have not received my letter or papers from you lately.
movements.notes: Savannah, Ga. At Uncle Henry's request, you went to Charlotte. Haven't received letters or papers. Not in very good health — hope improving. **JAMES'S NIGHT BLINDNESS** — "James says that since we came here, troubles him to see at night, but he can see as well as usual in the day time." Moved into city near river. Living in board shanties, 4 men each. **REGT. PAID** — sent $130 by express. Martin has $70. Soldier drunk — "meshed clothes with a woman and then walked down street with her. There were met by some soldiers who after pounding them, robbed each of them." **JULY 4TH** — dress parade, review, firing of cannon & ringing of bells. Parade of all fire companies — **"all black but one. The darkeys young and old all turned out."** **DR. JOHN SWEENEY** called — his brother James in charge of Division Hospital. John graduated medical school with Ranch Malcolm. Ranch was assistant surgeon — now discharged. John inquired about Frances. Tomatoes & green corn — homesick. James on duty, can't write.
Returned to Ogdensburg. Mustered out July 27, 1865.

movements.letterExcerpt: We reached here last Sat. and have been waiting for the Paymaster ever since. He has not come yet and I have some doubts whether I shall be able to be home this week. I am very anxious to see you all ...
movements.notes: Camp Wheeler, Ogdensburgh, N.Y. **THE HOMECOMING.** "We reached here last Sat. and have been waiting for the Paymaster ever since." Doesn't know if he'll be home this week. "I am very anxious to see you all again." **LUTHER** will come with him — "spend a short time at 'our house.'" Got stationery from "one of the boys who I guess does not like writing much." **P.S. — "We had a grand reception. I will tell you all about it at the tea table."** Stationery is a printed poem "Soldier's Letter" with fill-in spaces.
